short.en: Write text, download a PDF.

tools.meta_description: Create a PDF from your own text, free in your browser. Type or paste, then download a clean PDF with no sign-up.
steps: Type your text in the box, then choose Plain text or Markdown from the Mode list.
Pick a font, a font size, a page size and a margin; in Markdown mode, use # for headings, **bold**, - for lists and | tables |.
Optionally choose images to add at the end, then press Create & Download PDF and save ak-premium-created.pdf.

content.use: Create PDF turns typed text into a PDF file without any word processor or sign-up. A teacher types a short notice and downloads it as a PDF to share in a class group. A shop owner types a price list and sends it to customers. In plain-text mode the text flows across pages. In Markdown mode you can add headings, bold and italic words, bullet and numbered lists, and tables, which are drawn as real PDF tables. You can also attach images, which are added one per page at the end, and pick A4 or Letter paper with your own margin. Everything happens in your browser, so the text you type never leaves your device.
content.tip: Write Markdown with a blank line between blocks, and put tables in the | Header | Row | style with a | --- | --- | line under the header. Check the downloaded PDF once before sharing, because the tool does not show a preview first.
content.limit: Markdown rendering covers headings, paragraphs, bold, italic, code, lists, tables, quotes and horizontal rules. It does not keep pasted HTML formatting, footnotes, embedded links or coloured text, and tables with very long cells may wrap awkwardly. Images are added one per page at the end, not inside the text.
content.example: Typing '# Shop Notice', a short paragraph and a 2-column price table in Markdown mode and pressing Create & Download PDF gives a PDF with a large heading, the paragraph and a real table.
faq: Can I use headings and tables in Create PDF?

Yes, in Markdown mode. Use # for a heading, **bold** for bold words, - for a bullet list and a | table | with a | --- | line for tables. Plain-text mode sets everything in one font with no formatting.
Which Markdown is supported?
Headings, paragraphs, bold, italic, code, bullet and numbered lists, tables, blockquotes, code blocks and horizontal rules. Footnotes, HTML and coloured text are not supported.
Where do my images go in the PDF?
Images you choose are added one per page at the end of the document, fitted to the page with your margin. They cannot be placed inside the text.
What page sizes can I choose?
A4 or Letter. The margin can be set from 5 to 40 mm, and the font size from 8 to 20 points.

short.en: Turn images into one PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn JPG, PNG and WebP images into one PDF for free, in your browser. No upload and no sign-up needed.
steps: Choose one or more JPG, PNG or WebP images with the file button.
Pick how many images go on each page, the page size, margin, fit or fill, and the print DPI.
Leave auto-rotate on for phone photos, choose whether to keep or remove photo metadata, then press Convert Images to PDF.

content.use: Images to PDF turns photos and scans into a single PDF file. A student photographs handwritten notes and sends them as one PDF to a teacher. A shop owner photographs receipts and keeps them as one monthly PDF. A job applicant photographs certificates and attaches one PDF to an application. You can put one, two or four images on each page, pick A4 or Letter paper, and choose whether each image is fitted whole or cropped to fill its cell. Phone photos are rotated upright from their EXIF data, and you can set the print DPI and JPEG quality. The PDF is built in your browser, so your photos are never uploaded anywhere.
content.tip: For a print-ready result, pick 300 DPI and 95% JPEG quality. For a small file to send in a chat, pick 72 DPI and 70% quality. Leave auto-rotate on, or sideways phone photos stay sideways.
content.limit: Only JPG, PNG and WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. Re-encoding through the browser strips photo metadata; keeping the original file skips the rotation fix. Fill mode crops the edges of images to fit the cell. Very large batches may run slowly.
content.example: Choosing 4 photos, picking 4 per page and 150 DPI, and pressing Convert Images to PDF gives one 1-page PDF with the four photos in a two-by-two grid.
faq: How do 2 or 4 images per page work?
With 2 per page the images sit side by side; with 4 they form a two-by-two grid. Each image gets its own cell, and Fit shows the whole image while Fill crops it to cover the cell.
Why are my phone photos sideways, and how do I fix it?
Phone photos store their rotation in EXIF data. Leave 'Auto-rotate photos from EXIF data' ticked and the tool turns them upright. If you choose to keep the original file, the rotation fix is skipped.
What does the print DPI setting do?
It sets how large each image prints: an image prints at its pixels divided by the DPI in inches. 300 DPI is sharp print quality, 150 is good, and 72 is for screens.
Does the PDF keep my photo metadata?
No, unless you choose 'Keep the original file'. Re-encoding removes EXIF data such as the camera, date and location. Keeping the original keeps the metadata but skips auto-rotate.

short.en: Combine PDFs into one file.

steps: Choose two or more PDF files with the file button. Each one shows a thumbnail of its first page. You can add more files later and they join the list instead of replacing it.
Drag the thumbnails into the order you want. Under each file, type the pages to take, for example 1-3, 5, or leave it blank for all pages, and pick a rotation if a file is sideways.
Set Blank pages between files if you want a divider page after each file, then press Merge PDFs.
Download ak-premium-merged.pdf. Bookmarks from your files are kept and point at the right pages.

content.use: People merge PDFs when a report, invoice set or application form is split across several files and needs to be sent as one document. A teacher merges chapter PDFs into one handout, a shop owner merges daily bills into one monthly file, and a student merges assignment pages before uploading them to a portal. With page ranges you can take only the pages you need from each file, rotate a sideways scan upright as it is merged, and add a blank page between files as a divider. Bookmarks from your files are kept, so the merged PDF still has a working contents list.
content.tip: Type the pages under each file before you merge. A file with pages 1-3, 5 gives only those pages, and a sideways scan can be rotated upright in the same step, so check both boxes before pressing Merge PDFs.
content.limit: Merged PDFs keep the original pages as they are. The tool does not flatten forms, remove passwords from a protected file, or fix a damaged PDF. A protected PDF must be unlocked first. Bookmarks are kept only when the source file has them, and a bookmark for a page you did not pick is dropped.
content.example: Merging a 3-page invoice, a 2-page delivery note and a 1-page cover letter gives one 6-page PDF in that order. Taking only pages 1-3, 5 from the invoice instead gives a shorter file.
faq: Can I take only some pages from a file when I merge?
Yes. Type the pages in the Pages box under that file, for example 1-3, 5. Leave it blank to take all pages.
Can I rotate a file while merging it?
Yes. Use the Rotate list under a file to turn its pages 90, 180 or 270 degrees as they are merged. Pages that were already rotated keep their rotation plus the extra turn.
Are bookmarks kept when I merge PDFs?

Yes, when the files have them. Bookmarks from each file are kept in the merged PDF and point at the right pages. A file without bookmarks adds none, and a bookmark for a page you did not pick is dropped.
Can I add a blank page between files when merging?
Yes. Set Blank pages between files to 1 or more, up to 5. A blank page is added after each file except the last, sized like the page before it.

tools.meta_description: Merge multiple PDF files into one PDF for free, in your browser. Pick pages per file, rotate, add blank pages and keep bookmarks.

short.en: Split by pages, chapters or size.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick a Mode: Page ranges, Extract every page, Split by bookmarks, Every N pages, Split into equal parts, or Split by file size.
Fill in the box for your mode: ranges like 1-3, 5, 8-10, the pages per part, the number of parts, or the largest size per part in MB.
Press Split PDF. Bookmarks mode needs a file with bookmarks; files without them should use Page ranges.
Download the result: one PDF for Page ranges, or a ZIP file with one PDF per part for the other modes.

content.use: Splitting is for the opposite job: taking only the pages you need out of a long PDF. A student extracts chapters 2 and 3 from a 200-page book, a manager pulls one contract clause out of a full agreement, and a shop owner separates one month’s invoices from a yearly file. You can split at the bookmarks so each chapter becomes its own file, cut the document into equal parts for sharing, take every fifth page for a sample, or split by size so no part is bigger than your email limit. Each part downloads in one ZIP file.
content.tip: Use Split by bookmarks for a book with chapters, and Split by file size when an email or portal refuses a big file. Check the part names in the ZIP before you send them.
content.limit: Split pages keep their original content and formatting. The tool cannot split a password-protected PDF, and it does not rebuild text from a scanned page. Splitting by bookmarks needs a file with bookmarks, and splitting by size keeps a single page whole even when that page alone is over the limit.
content.example: Splitting a 12-chapter book by bookmarks gives 12 PDFs, one per chapter, named after the chapter. Splitting the same file into 3 equal parts gives parts of 4 pages each.
faq: How do I split a PDF at its chapters?
Choose Split by bookmarks. The tool reads the bookmarks in the file and makes one PDF per chapter, named after the bookmark. Files without bookmarks need Page ranges instead.
Can I split a PDF into equal parts?
Yes. Choose Split into equal parts and set the number of parts. A 10-page PDF split into 3 parts gives parts of 4, 3 and 3 pages.
Can I split a PDF so no part is bigger than 5 MB?
Yes. Choose Split by file size and set the largest size per part. Pages are grouped until the limit is reached. One very large page is kept whole even if it is over the limit.
What is the difference between Every N pages and Extract every page?
Extract every page makes one PDF per page. Every N pages groups pages, so every 5 pages gives one PDF with pages 1-5, one with 6-10, and so on.

tools.meta_description: Split a PDF by page range, bookmarks, equal parts or file size, free in your browser. No upload, no sign-up.

short.en: Reorder, rotate and delete pages.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.

Drag the page thumbnails into the order you want. Use Rotate 90 on a sideways page, Duplicate to copy a page, Split in two to cut one page into a left and a right page, Blank after to add an empty page, and Delete to drop a page. Tick Select on pages to save only those.
Press Reorder PDF to download the organised file, or Download selected pages to save just the ticked pages.

content.use: Organizing a PDF is for fixing page order after scanning or merging: a scanned book with two pages swapped, a report with the appendix in the wrong place, or a set of pages that were merged in the wrong order. Thumbnails show every page, so you can see what you are moving instead of guessing by number. You can also split one wide page into a left and a right page, add a blank page where a divider belongs, copy a page that is needed twice, or save only the pages you ticked as a separate file. Your original file is never changed; the result downloads as a new PDF.
content.tip: Split in two cuts a page down the middle, which suits a scanned double-page spread. Blank after is handy for a divider page before a new chapter. Tick Select on the pages you need and use Download selected pages when you only want part of the file.
content.limit: Organizing reorders, rotates, duplicates, splits and deletes pages. It does not edit the text or images on a page. Splitting cuts a page into a left and a right half, not into top and bottom, and a split page keeps the same rotation on both halves. Blank pages are plain white with the size of the page before them.
content.example: Moving page 3 to the front of a 5-page PDF, splitting a wide scanned spread on page 2 into two pages, and deleting page 5 gives a clean 6-page file.
faq: Can I split one page into two pages?
Yes. Press Split in two on the page thumbnail. The page is cut down the middle into a left page and a right page. Press it again to undo the split before you download.
How do I save only some pages?
Tick Select on the thumbnails you want, then press Download selected pages. The rest of the file is left out of the download.
Can I add a blank page?
Yes. Press Blank after on a page thumbnail to add an empty page right after it. The blank page is the same size as the page before it.
Does duplicating a page copy its rotation too?
Yes. A duplicated page keeps the rotation of the page it was copied from. You can rotate the copy on its own afterwards if you need it the other way up.

tools.meta_description: Reorder, split, duplicate and extract PDF pages in your browser. Drag thumbnails, add blank pages and download the organised file.

short.en: Delete selected pages and keep the rest.

tools.meta_description: Delete pages from a PDF by clicking thumbnails, searching text or finding blank pages. Free in your browser, no upload.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.

Click the page thumbnails to pick the pages to remove, or type the page numbers in the box, for example 2, 4-5. Use Select blank pages to find empty pages, or Find pages with this text to pick every page that contains a word.
Press Remove Pages and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Remove Pages deletes pages you do not need from a PDF and downloads the rest as a new file. A student removes blank pages from scanned notes before uploading them. An office worker removes a draft page from a report before sending it to a client. You can click the page thumbnails to pick pages by sight, search for every page that contains a word, or ask the tool to find blank pages for you. You can also list pages by number, using commas and ranges such as 2, 4-5, and the tool checks every number against the real page count before it removes anything. Your original file is never changed; the result is a separate download.
content.tip: Click a thumbnail to select a page, and click it again to undo. Select blank pages only picks pages with no text and no ink, so a page with a stamp or a photo is kept. Search is not case sensitive.
content.limit: You must keep at least one page; the tool refuses to remove every page. Page numbers that do not exist in the file are rejected with a message. Blank-page detection looks for text and ink, so a page with a faint mark or a stamp may not count as blank. The tool only removes whole pages. It does not delete text inside a page or fix a damaged PDF.
content.example: In a 10-page report, clicking the thumbnails of pages 2, 4 and 5 and pressing Remove Pages downloads a 7-page PDF with those pages gone.
faq: How do I pick pages by sight instead of by number?
Choose the file and click the page thumbnails. A clicked page is marked as selected and its number appears in the page list box. Click it again to undo.
What counts as a blank page?
A page with no text and no ink at all. A page with a stamp, a photo, a logo or even a faint mark is not counted as blank, so it is kept.
Can I remove every page that contains a word?
Yes. Type the word in the search box and press Select matching pages. Every page whose text contains that word is selected, and you can remove them all at once.
What happens if I type a page number that does not exist?
The tool checks your list against the real page count and shows an error, such as page 12 being outside 1 to 10. Nothing is removed until the list is valid.

short.en: Rotate all pages 90, 180, or 270 degrees.

tools.meta_description: Rotate PDF pages one by one, auto-rotate by text direction, or straighten a tilted scan. Free in your browser, no upload.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.

Pick an angle on each page thumbnail, or leave the Angle list to turn every page the same way. Use Auto-rotate by text direction to let the tool work out which pages are upside down, or Straighten a tilted scan for a crooked page.
Press Rotate PDF and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Rotate PDF turns pages of a PDF by 90, 180 or 270 degrees, which fixes files that open sideways or upside down. A student rotates scanned notes that were photographed sideways. You can turn each page on its own using the thumbnails, or turn every page at once with the Angle list. If you are not sure which way a page goes, Auto-rotate checks the text direction and sets the angle for you. A scan that is only slightly tilted can be straightened too. Rotation adds to each page's existing turn, so a page already at 90 degrees becomes 180 if you turn it again. The result downloads as a new PDF and your original file stays unchanged.
content.tip: Use Auto-rotate by text direction when a scan mixes upright and upside-down pages; it sets each page on its own. For a page that is only slightly crooked, use Straighten a tilted scan instead of guessing an angle.
content.limit: Rotation turns pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees. Straighten a tilted scan only fixes a tilt of up to 6 degrees, and a straightened page is rebuilt as an image, so its text is no longer selectable. Auto-rotate reads the text direction, so it cannot help on a page with no text at all. The tool does not straighten a page tilted more than 6 degrees.
content.example: A 5-page scan with two upside-down pages is fixed by pressing Auto-rotate by text direction and then Rotate PDF, which downloads all 5 pages the right way up.
faq: Can I rotate just one page?
Yes. Choose the file and set the angle on that page's thumbnail. The other pages keep the angle shown on their own thumbnails.
How does Auto-rotate know which way is up?
It reads the text on each page and works out whether the letters are upright, sideways or upside down, then sets that page's angle. A page with no text, such as a photo page, is left as it is.
Can Rotate PDF straighten a crooked scan?
Only a small tilt, up to 6 degrees. Press Straighten a tilted scan. A straightened page is rebuilt as an image, so you can no longer select its text.
Why did my page turn 180 degrees when I chose 90?
The rotation adds to the page's existing rotation. A page already turned 90 degrees becomes 180 degrees when you rotate it by 90 again.

short.en: Number pages your way.

tools.meta_description: Add page numbers to a PDF, free in your browser. Choose the position, font, size, colour, format and starting number.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick the Position, Font, Size and Colour. Choose how the number reads: a plain number, Page 3, or Page 3 of 12.
Set Start numbering at, Skip first pages for a cover, and First pages in roman numerals for front matter.
Press Add Page Numbers and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Add Page Numbers stamps a number on every page you choose in a PDF, so long documents are easy to follow and refer to. A teacher numbers a 40-page handout so students can find the right page in class. A student numbers an assignment before uploading it to a portal. An office worker numbers a report so page references in a meeting make sense. You choose where the number sits, the font, size and colour, and whether it reads as a plain number, Page 3, or Page 3 of 12. You can skip a cover page, start at any number, and number the front pages in roman numerals.
content.tip: Number the final version of your document. If you edit the PDF afterwards and add or remove pages, the numbers will no longer match, so run the tool again on the edited file.
content.limit: Numbers are stamped on top of the page, so they may sit over a footer that is already there. The tool numbers pages in order and cannot put two different numbers on one page.
content.example: Numbering a 12-page report with Position set to Bottom right and Format set to Page 3 of 12 puts Page 1 of 12 on the first page and Page 12 of 12 on the last.
faq: Can I put the number at the top of the page?
Yes. Choose Top left, Top centre or Top right in the Position list. Bottom centre is the default.
Can I number pages as Page 3 of 12?
Yes. Choose Page 1 of 12 in the Number format list. The total is the number of pages in the file.
How do I number the first pages with roman numerals?
Set First pages in roman numerals to how many front pages you have, for example 3 for i, ii, iii. The pages after them count in normal numbers from your starting number.
Can I start numbering at 5 and skip the cover?
Yes. Set Skip first pages to 1 for the cover and Start numbering at to 5. The cover gets no number and numbering starts at 5 on the next page.

short.en: Stamp text or a logo on pages.

tools.meta_description: Stamp a text or logo watermark on PDF pages, free in your browser. Choose angle, colour, opacity and pages. Your file stays on your device.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick Text or Image in the Watermark type list. For text, type it in the Watermark text box (under 60 characters). For a logo, choose a PNG or JPG file and its size.
Set the Angle, Size and Colour, and move the Opacity slider. Tick Repeat the watermark across the page for a tiled text watermark.
Pick which pages get the mark: All pages, Odd pages only, Even pages only, or a Page range like 1-3, 5.
Press Add Watermark and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Add Watermark stamps your text or logo across the pages of a PDF, so readers can see at a glance that a document is a draft, a sample or confidential. A teacher stamps DRAFT on exam papers before sharing them. An office worker stamps CONFIDENTIAL on a report before sending it outside the company. A designer stamps SAMPLE on a portfolio file. You type the text or pick a logo, choose the angle, size, colour and opacity, and decide whether it repeats across the page or sits once in the middle. You can also stamp only the odd pages, the even pages, or a page range you type.
content.tip: Keep the text short, such as DRAFT or SAMPLE, because long text is harder to read at an angle. Use a low opacity for a faint mark that stays out of the way, and a high opacity when the mark must be obvious.
content.limit: The watermark text must be under 60 characters. A watermark is a visible mark only. It does not password-protect the file or stop someone from copying the text. Tiled repeat works for text watermarks; a logo is stamped once in the middle of each page. A logo keeps its shape, so a very wide logo is scaled to the page width you set.
content.example: Typing CONFIDENTIAL, choosing 35% opacity and pressing Add Watermark stamps CONFIDENTIAL diagonally on every page of a 6-page report. Choosing a logo instead stamps the logo in the middle of each page.
faq: Can I use my logo as a watermark instead of text?
Yes. Choose Image in the Watermark type list and pick a PNG or JPG logo. Set the logo size as a percentage of the page width.
Can I change the watermark angle and colour?
Yes. Set the angle from -90 to 90 degrees and pick any colour. The old fixed 45-degree grey mark is now only the default.
Can I watermark only some pages?
Yes. Choose Odd pages only, Even pages only, or Page range and type the pages, for example 1-3, 5. All pages is the default.
Can I repeat the watermark across the whole page?
Yes, for text watermarks. Tick Repeat the watermark across the page and the text is stamped in a grid. A logo is stamped once in the middle of each page.

short.en: Add text to one page.

tools.meta_description: Add wrapped text to a PDF page with font matching and white-out corrections. Free in your browser, no upload.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.

Type the text in 'Text to add', then set the Page number, choose a Position, a Font and an Alignment, and set the text box width. Tick 'White-out the area behind the new text' to cover what was there first.
Press Add Text to PDF and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Edit PDF adds text to one page of a PDF, for small fixes such as a missing heading, a note or a date. A teacher adds a class name to a handout, an office worker adds 'Approved' to a memo, and a student adds a title to an assignment. You pick the page, the position, the font and the alignment. Long text wraps inside your box instead of running off the edge, and the font list matches the fonts already on the page. If the old wording is wrong, white-out the area behind the new text first, so the correction sits on a clean patch. The rest of the page is left exactly as it was.
content.tip: Leave the text box width at 0 to use the full page width. Set a narrower width to keep the text in a column. White-out only covers the box your new text sits in, so place the text right over the words you want to hide.
content.limit: The tool adds new text only. It cannot truly edit or delete text that is already in the PDF: white-out paints a white box over the old words, but they are still in the file underneath, so it is not safe for hiding sensitive details. Removing old text from the file itself needs a desktop PDF editor. The added text goes on one page at a time, in a built-in font at 12, 18, 24 or 36 points. A single very long word can still run past the edge of its box.
content.example: Adding the text 'Class 10-A' to page 1 at the top centre in size 24 puts a clear heading on the first page of a handout, and ticking white-out first covers the old heading underneath.
faq: Can I edit text that is already in the PDF?
No. Edit PDF only adds new text on top of a page. It cannot change or delete existing text, so fix typos in the original document and export a fresh PDF.
What does white-out do, exactly?
It paints a white box over the area your new text sits in, so the old words cannot be seen. The old text is still in the file underneath the box, so do not use it to hide anything sensitive.
Why does my long text wrap onto two lines now?
The text wraps inside the box width you set, so it no longer runs off the edge of the page. Set a wider box, or a smaller font size, to fit it on one line.
Can I add text to several pages at once?
No. Each run adds text to one page only. Repeat the steps for each page you need to mark.

short.en: Reduce PDF size — lossless, balanced or small.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick a level: Lossless only re-saves the file and never touches quality, Balanced shrinks photos to 150 DPI, Small shrinks photos to 96 DPI. Text stays as text on every level.
Set the JPEG quality if you want, press Compress PDF and download the result.

content.use: A PDF that is too large to email or upload is the usual reason to compress one. Admission forms, job applications and WhatsApp forwards often have a file-size limit, and a compressed copy is what gets through. Compressing also helps when a PDF is stored on a phone with little free space. Photos inside the PDF are what make it large, so this tool shrinks the photos and leaves the text alone.
content.tip: Start with Lossless if the PDF is mostly text and you only want a smaller file with no quality change. Use Balanced for a PDF with photos, and Small only when size matters more than photo quality. Lower the JPEG quality slider a little at a time and check the result.
content.limit: Only photos inside the PDF are re-encoded; text, vector drawings and scanned pages are never re-rendered, so the text stays selectable and searchable on every level. Lossless only re-saves the file, so it helps little on image-heavy PDFs. Photos that are already small, masked images and unusual image formats are left unchanged and counted in the result. Compression cannot fix a damaged PDF.
content.example: A 12 MB PDF with photos often drops to about 4 MB on Balanced and under 2 MB on Small, depending on the images. A text-only PDF may shrink by only a few percent on Lossless.
faq: Does compression change my text?
No. Photos inside the PDF are re-encoded at a smaller size, but the text is never turned into an image. It stays selectable, copyable and searchable on every level, including Small.
What is the difference between the three levels?

Lossless only re-saves the file with tighter object streams and removes unused objects, so nothing changes in quality. Balanced shrinks photos to 150 DPI, which is fine for screens and most printing. Small shrinks photos to 96 DPI for the smallest file. The JPEG quality slider applies to Balanced and Small.
Why is my compressed PDF still large?
Only photos are shrunk. If the PDF is mostly text or vector graphics, or its photos are already small, there is little left to save. The result line tells you which images were skipped and why.
How do I know how much was saved?
The result line shows the old size and the new size, with the percentage saved. If the file grew instead, it says how much larger it is.

tools.meta_description: Compress a PDF and reduce its file size, free in your browser. Photos are shrunk, text stays selectable. Lossless, balanced or small.

short.en: Layout-aware text extraction: columns, headings, order.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick Plain text, Markdown or CSV (tables) as the output format.
Press Extract Text.
Save the downloaded file, which lists the text page by page.
tools.meta_description: Extract text from a PDF with layout awareness: columns kept in reading order, headings marked, and tables as CSV, free in your browser.

content.use: PDF to Text pulls the words out of a PDF and saves them as a file, using the position of each word on the page to keep the reading order. A student extracts a two-column newsletter and gets the left column first, then the right, instead of lines mixed together. An office worker extracts a report as Markdown, where large text becomes headings. A clerk extracts the tables from a statement as CSV, with the columns kept.
content.tip: Markdown mode marks text that is clearly larger than the body text as a heading, which makes long documents easier to scan. CSV mode exports the tables the tool detects, one table per file section, with the columns kept. If the order looks wrong, try the plain text format and check a few lines against the PDF.
content.limit: The tool only reads PDFs that already have a text layer. A scanned-image PDF with no text layer gives no text, and the tool says so. Tables, columns and layout are kept from word positions, so a very unusual layout, rotated text or a complicated design may still read in the wrong order; check the result before you trust it.
content.example: Extracting text from a two-column newsletter downloads ak-premium-text.txt with the left column first and the right column second, each page starting with a '--- Page N ---' marker. In Markdown mode the same file marks the article titles as headings.
faq: Does the text keep the page layout?

Yes, as far as word positions allow. The tool reads the position of each word, so a two-column page comes out left column first, then right column, instead of lines mixed together. The exact page design is not kept.
How does the Markdown format work?
Markdown mode marks text that is clearly larger than the body text as a heading, keeps paragraphs in order, and marks each page. It is plain Markdown you can paste into a document or a notes app.
Can I extract tables as a spreadsheet?
Yes. Choose CSV (tables) as the format and the tool exports the tables it detects, with the columns kept, as comma-separated values you can open in Excel or Google Sheets.
Why is the reading order wrong in my PDF?

The tool guesses the reading order from word positions. A page with sidebars, boxes, rotated text or an unusual design can confuse that guess. Check the result against the PDF, and try the plain text format if the Markdown or CSV order looks wrong.

short.en: Render pages as PNG images.

tools.meta_description: Render PDF pages as PNG images and download them, free in your browser. No upload, no sign-up.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick a resolution from 72 to 300 DPI, a format (PNG, JPEG or WebP), and the pages you want, or leave it as all.
Tick Grayscale or Transparent background if you need them, press Convert Pages to Images, then download each page or the whole set as one ZIP.

content.use: PDF to Images turns pages of a PDF into pictures, so you can share a single page in a chat, add it to a slide or post it online. A teacher turns one page of a worksheet into a PNG to share in a class group. A student turns a diagram page into a PNG to paste into an assignment. You can pick the resolution from 72 to 300 DPI, choose PNG, JPEG or WebP, export only the pages you need, and make grayscale images or PNGs with a transparent background. A single page downloads as one image with no ZIP. The work happens in your browser.
content.tip: For a sharp image to print, pick 300 DPI PNG. For a small image to send in a chat, pick 150 DPI JPEG. If you only need one page, type its number in the Pages box instead of converting the whole file.
content.limit: Each page becomes a separate picture, so a 50-page PDF gives 50 images and one ZIP. The pictures show the page, not editable text. Transparent background only works for PNG, and only where the page itself has no background. A very large PDF at 300 DPI may be slow or run out of browser memory.
content.example: Converting pages 1-2 of a 5-page worksheet at 150 DPI as PNG gives two image links, one per page, and no ZIP, because only two pages were chosen.
faq: What DPI should I pick?
72 DPI is a quick preview, 150 DPI is good for sharing and slides, and 300 DPI is print quality. Higher DPI means sharper images but bigger files and a slower conversion.
Can I export only some pages?
Yes. Type the pages in the Pages box, for example 1-3, 5, or leave it as all. If you pick exactly one page, you get a single image link and no ZIP file.
How does the transparent background work?
Tick 'Transparent background' with PNG output and the page is rendered without its usual white background, so parts of the page with no content stay transparent. It only works for PNG.
Can I make WebP or grayscale images?
Yes. Pick WebP in the format list for small files, and tick Grayscale to turn every page into shades of grey. Grayscale works with PNG, JPEG and WebP.

short.en: Draw a signature, stamp a PDF, or digitally sign it.

tools.meta_description: Draw a signature and download it as a PNG, stamp it onto a PDF, or digitally sign a PDF with your own .p12 certificate, free in your browser.
steps: Draw your signature on the canvas with your mouse or finger, or type your name and press Use Typed Signature.
Press Download Signature PNG to save the signature, or Clear Signature to start again.
To stamp it onto a PDF, choose the PDF, pick the pages, position and width, then press Sign PDF & Download.
To digitally sign a PDF with a certificate, choose the PDF, choose your .p12 certificate file, type its password, then press Digitally Sign PDF.

content.use: e-Sign lets you draw a signature on a blank canvas and download it as a PNG, stamp it onto chosen pages of a PDF at a chosen spot, or digitally sign a PDF with your own .p12 certificate. A shop owner signs a delivery note by drawing on a phone screen. A freelancer stamps a typed signature onto the last page of an invoice. A student digitally signs a form with a self-signed certificate. The stamp is a picture of your signature; the digital signature is a real cryptographic signature inside the PDF.
content.tip: Draw slowly and in one smooth motion for the cleanest line. For stamping, the bottom right of the last page is the usual place for a signature. For the digital signature, you need your own .p12 or .pfx certificate file and its password; both stay in your browser and are never uploaded.
content.limit: The stamp is a picture of your signature, not a certificate-based signature. The digital signature is self-signed: it proves the PDF was signed with your certificate, but a PDF reader will show it as not trusted until your certificate is trusted, because no trusted authority issued it. A .p12 file with a long certificate chain may not fit the signature field. A blank canvas will not download.
content.example: Drawing a signature and pressing Download Signature PNG saves ak-premium-signature.png. Stamping it on the last page of a one-page invoice downloads ak-premium-signed.pdf. Digitally signing the same PDF with a .p12 file downloads ak-premium-digitally-signed.pdf, and a PDF reader shows a signature panel for it.
faq: What is the difference between stamping and digitally signing?

Stamping places a picture of your signature onto the PDF pages, like signing with a pen. Digitally signing adds a cryptographic signature with your .p12 certificate, which a PDF reader can check to confirm the file was signed with that certificate and not changed afterwards.
Where do I get a .p12 certificate file?

A .p12 file holds your private key and certificate. You can make a self-signed one with OpenSSL on your computer, or export one from a certificate you already own. AK Premium does not make or store certificates for you.
Why does my PDF reader say the signature is not trusted?

The signature is self-signed, not issued by a trusted certificate authority, so readers show it as signed by your own certificate but not trusted. That is normal for a self-signed certificate; it still proves the file was signed with your certificate.
Is my certificate password sent anywhere?
No. Your .p12 file and its password are read only in your browser to make the signature, and they are never uploaded or sent to any server.

short.en: Remove the password from a PDF you own.

steps: Choose the protected PDF with the file button. You can choose several files at once if they share one password.
Press Check Protection to see whether the file is locked, which password it needs and what is locked.
Type the exact password, including capital letters, then press Unlock PDF.
Download the ordinary PDF that opens without a password. For several files, the unlocked copies download as one ZIP file.

content.use: Unlocking is for a PDF you own and know the password for, but no longer want to type every time you open it. It is also the way to get a clean copy of a protected file for printing or for a tool that does not accept protected PDFs. Before you unlock, Check Protection tells you whether the file is locked at all, whether your password is the user or the owner password, and what the file locks, such as printing or copying. You can unlock several files at once when they share one password, and the unlocked copies download together in one ZIP file.
content.tip: Make sure you type the exact password, including capital letters. A wrong password gives a clear wrong-password message, not a broken file. Press Check Protection first if you want to know which password you typed and what the file locks.
content.limit: The tool does real standard PDF decryption and keeps the original pages and layout. It does not guess or crack passwords, and it cannot unlock a file whose password you do not know. Batch unlocking tries one password for every file, so a file with a different password is skipped.
content.example: Unlocking a protected fee receipt gives you an ordinary PDF that opens without a password. Checking protection first shows it was locked with AES-256 and that copying was not allowed.
faq: How do I see what a protected PDF locks before I unlock it?
Press Check Protection. It tells you whether the file is locked, whether your password is the user or owner password, the encryption type, and what is locked, such as printing or copying.
What is the difference between the user password and the owner password?
The user password opens the file. The owner password also opens it and can change the permissions. Check Protection tells you which one you typed.
Can I unlock several PDFs at once?
Yes, if they all share the same password. Choose several files and press Unlock PDF. The unlocked files download as one ZIP. Files with a different password are skipped and named in the message.
Does unlocking tell me what was locked?
Yes. If you press Check Protection first, the unlocked message also says which password opened the file and what was locked before, such as copying or editing.

tools.meta_description: Unlock a PDF in your browser. Check its protection first, then remove the password. Your file stays on your device.

short.en: Lock a PDF with a password (AES-256).

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Type a password you can remember. There is no way to recover it if you forget it. Add an owner password if it should be different.
Choose what readers may do: printing quality, copying text, filling in forms, adding comments, assembling pages and other changes. Copying and editing are off by default.
Press Protect PDF and download the encrypted file. It opens in any PDF reader with the password.

content.use: Protecting a PDF is for files that should only be opened by someone who knows the password: a salary slip, a contract draft, a fee receipt or a report with personal details. The password travels with the file, so it works in Acrobat and Chrome without any account. You can set a separate owner password, allow printing at full or low quality, and choose whether readers may copy text, fill in forms, add comments, assemble pages or change anything else. Copying and editing are off by default, so a protected file stays read-only unless you switch a permission on.
content.tip: Use a password you can remember or store safely, because there is no way to recover it. A password of 8 or more characters with letters and numbers is much harder to guess than a short word. Leave copying and editing off unless the reader truly needs them.
content.limit: The tool uses standard AES-256 PDF encryption (qpdf, revision 6). It does not stop someone from photographing the screen or re-sharing the file once they have opened it, and a forgotten password cannot be recovered by this site. Screen-reader access always stays on. Certificate-based encryption for named people is not supported.
content.example: Protecting a salary slip with a password means only the person who knows that password can open it in a PDF reader. Leaving copying off means the reader can print it but cannot copy the text.
faq: Can I allow printing but stop copying?
Yes. Printing is allowed by default and copying is off. Tick Allow copying text and images only if you want copying too.
What is the owner password for?

It opens the file like the user password, and it is the password that controls the permissions. Leave it blank to use the same password for both. Use a different one if someone else should open the file but not change its permissions.
Can I let people fill in forms but not change anything else?
Yes. Tick Allow filling in forms and leave Allow any other changes unticked. Forms can be filled in, but the rest of the document cannot be changed.
Does Protect PDF stop screen readers?
No. Screen-reader access always stays on, so the file remains readable by assistive technology. It is the one permission that cannot be switched off.

tools.meta_description: Protect a PDF with a password in your browser. AES-256 encryption, with printing, copying and editing permissions you choose. Files stay on your device.

short.en: Crop margins on every page.

tools.meta_description: Crop PDF margins per side, per page or to A4, Letter or square, with a visual preview. Free in your browser, no upload.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Set the margin for each side, or pick a shape such as A4, Letter or Square. Use Show crop preview to drag the crop box on page 1, or Remove white borders to trim every page to its ink.
Choose All pages or a Page range, then press Crop PDF and save the downloaded copy.

content.use: Crop PDF trims the edges off the pages of a PDF, which removes wide white borders from scanned pages. A student crops the borders off scanned notes so they read better on a phone, and a teacher crops a worksheet so the questions fill more of the page. You can set a different margin per side, crop only some pages, or cut every page to A4, Letter or a square. The preview shows page 1 so you can drag the crop box into place, and Remove white borders trims each page to the ink on it. The text in the middle of the page is never touched, and your original file stays unchanged.
content.tip: Use Show crop preview to see the result before you crop; dragging the box fills in the four margin boxes for you. Remove white borders is the quickest fix for a scan with uneven borders.
content.limit: Cropping only hides the trimmed area by moving the crop box; the content outside it stays in the file, so it is not a way to remove sensitive details. Each page keeps at least 10 points of width and height. The preview shows page 1 only, but the crop applies to the pages you chose. A page with no ink is left unchanged by Remove white borders.
content.example: Cropping a scanned worksheet with a 36-point margin on every side trims about half an inch of white border from the pages, and Remove white borders trims a form to the exact edge of its printed text.
faq: Can I crop only the top of the page?
Yes. Set the Top margin and leave the other three at 0. Each side has its own box.
What is a point?
A point is a printing unit. 72 points make one inch, so the default 36 points is about half an inch of margin on each side.
Can I crop a single page?
Yes. Choose Page range and type the page, for example 3. Only that page is cropped.
Does cropping delete the trimmed part for good?
No. Cropping moves the crop box, so the trimmed area is hidden but still in the file. Do not use it to hide sensitive details.

short.en: Permanently cover matching text in black.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick what to redact: exact text, or a pattern such as email addresses, phone numbers, CNIC numbers, IBAN numbers or dates. Tick 'Also check scanned pages (OCR)' if the PDF is a scan.
Press Redact and download the PDF. Open it in a PDF reader to confirm the covered text cannot be selected.

content.use: Redaction is for removing sensitive details before a document is shared: a CNIC number, a phone number, a bank account number or an email address. It is used when a document must be shared but a few details must not be seen. You can type the exact text, or pick a pattern and let the tool find every email address, phone number, CNIC number, IBAN or date. Where the text can be found, it is removed from the text itself and covered with a black box, so the page keeps its text layer. Where that is not possible, the page is rebuilt as an image with the box burned in. Scanned pages can be checked with OCR too.
content.tip: Use a pattern instead of typing each number by hand: CNIC finds every number shaped like 35202-1234567-1 in one pass. Check the downloaded PDF before you share it, and open it in a PDF reader to confirm the covered text cannot be selected or copied.
content.limit: Redaction works best on PDFs with a real text layer. Where the text is stored plainly, it is removed from the file and the page keeps its text layer. Where the text is split across the file or stored in an unusual way, that page is rebuilt as an image with the box burned in, so its text can no longer be selected. Scanned pages need the OCR box ticked, and OCR can miss faint or handwritten text. Always check the result before sharing.
content.example: Picking the CNIC pattern on a form covers every number shaped like 35202-1234567-1 with a black box in one pass, without typing any of them.
faq: Is the redacted text really gone, or just covered?

Where the tool can find the text in the file, it is removed from the text itself and the page keeps its text layer. Where it cannot, that page is rebuilt as an image with the box burned in, so the text cannot be selected. Check the downloaded file before you share it.
Can I redact a scanned PDF?
Yes, tick 'Also check scanned pages (OCR)'. The tool reads the pages and covers the matching words. OCR can miss faint or handwritten text, so check every page.
What do the patterns find?

Email finds addresses like name@example.com. Phone finds Pakistani mobile numbers and international numbers. CNIC finds numbers shaped like 35202-1234567-1. IBAN finds bank account numbers starting with two letters. Date finds dates like 12/03/2026.
Does the search care about capital letters?
No. The match ignores capitals, so typing cnic finds CNIC and Cnic. It matches part of a word too, so check the result before sharing.

tools.meta_description: Redact emails, phone numbers, CNIC and IBAN in a PDF, with OCR for scanned pages. Free in your browser, no upload.

short.en: Archive-style copy with metadata.

tools.meta_description: Make an archive-style PDF/A copy of your PDF, free in your browser. Adds archive metadata and reports six local archive checks.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Type a title in the 'Title' box, or leave it blank to use 'Archive document'.
Read the checklist under the button: it reports the title, author, creation date, fonts, page size and text layer as passed or failed.
Press Make Archive Copy and save the downloaded file.
Keep a copy of the original too, in case you need the untouched file later.

content.use: PDF to PDF/A makes an archive-style copy of a PDF with a title, author and creation date set, so the file is tidier for long-term storage, and it checks the file against six local archive checks before it saves. An office worker archives old reports with a clear title and author. A student archives assignments so they are easy to find years later. A shop owner archives invoices with a proper title instead of a scanner's file name. The checklist reports whether the file has a title, an author, a creation date, embedded fonts, one page size and a text layer on every page. Your original file stays untouched.
content.tip: Type a clear title that says what the file is, such as 'Sales report March 2026', because the title is what shows up in search and in PDF readers. If a checklist item fails, fix it in the program that made the PDF — for example export with fonts embedded — then run this tool again.
content.limit: This is an archive-style copy with a local checklist, not a certified PDF/A validation. The tool sets the title, author, subject and keywords and re-saves the file. It checks the file for a title, an author, a creation date, embedded fonts, one page size and a text layer, and reports each check as passed or failed. It does not embed fonts, convert colours or fix a failing check, and it does not turn scanned images into text.
content.example: Typing 'Invoice March 2026' as the title and pressing Make Archive Copy downloads a copy of the invoice with that title stored in it, and the checklist reports 5 of 6 checks passed because the invoice has no author set.
faq: Is the result a real certified PDF/A file?

No. The tool sets title, author, subject and keywords, re-saves the file and reports six local checks, but it does not validate the file against the PDF/A standard and does not claim to. A certified check needs a dedicated validator.
What does the checklist check?

Six things on your file: a title is set, an author is set, a creation date is set, the fonts are embedded, all pages are the same size, and every page has a text layer. Each one is reported as passed or failed, with a count such as 5 of 6.
What if a checklist item fails?

The copy is still made with the title you typed. A failed item tells you what to fix in the program that made the PDF — for example export it with fonts embedded, or set the author — then run the tool again.
Who is listed as the author?
The author is set to AK Premium, because the copy is made by this tool. The title is yours to choose.

short.en: Re-save a damaged PDF, best effort.

tools.meta_description: Try to repair a damaged PDF with a qpdf rebuild, free in your browser. Best-effort recovery with a per-page report of what was saved.
steps: Choose the damaged PDF file with the file button.
Press Repair PDF. The tool tries the qpdf rebuild first, then a re-save, then a text-and-image rebuild.
Read the report under the button: it says what was recovered and what was lost on each page.
Save the downloaded file and check it opens before you send it on.

content.use: Repair PDF tries to rescue a PDF that will not open, which happens when a download stops halfway or a file is copied badly. A student repairs an assignment PDF that a portal refuses to open. An office worker repairs a report that shows an error in the reader. A shop owner repairs an invoice that a customer cannot open. The tool first tries to rebuild the file with qpdf, then re-saves it as it is. If both fail, it pulls out any readable text and images and rebuilds a simple PDF from them, and reports what was recovered and what was lost on each page. Some files cannot be saved.
content.tip: Keep the damaged original file and work on a copy. If the repair gives you a rebuilt PDF, check that the important pages and numbers are there before you send it on, and read the per-page report to see which pages lost their layout.
content.limit: Repair is best effort only. A file with no readable content cannot be fixed, and the tool will say it could not repair the file. When it falls back to rebuilding from text and images, the layout, tables and fonts are lost; only the words and pictures survive. A password-protected file must be unlocked first.
content.example: A half-downloaded 8-page report that will not open is repaired by the qpdf rebuild, and the download gives back all 8 pages in a working PDF, with the report saying the text layer is present on every page.
faq: What does Repair PDF try first?

It tries to rebuild the file with qpdf, which fixes broken file structure such as a damaged table of contents. If that fails it tries a plain re-save, and if that fails too it rebuilds a PDF from any readable text and images.
What is the rebuilt PDF made from?
Any text and images the tool can still read from the damaged file. The layout, tables and fonts are lost, but the words and pictures are saved on plain pages.
Can Repair PDF fix a password-protected file?
No. A protected file must be unlocked first. Repair cannot read a file it cannot open.
Will the repaired file look the same as the original?
A qpdf rebuild or a re-save looks the same. A rebuilt PDF is plain text and images on plain pages. Check the result before you send it.

short.en: Compare text in two PDFs.

tools.meta_description: Compare two PDFs word by word with added and removed highlighting, free in your browser. Visual page diff and a downloadable report.
steps: Choose the first PDF with the first file button.
Choose the second PDF with the second file button.
Press Compare PDFs and read the word diff: added words in green, removed words in red.
Read the two lists under it — lines only in the first PDF, and lines only in the second — and the visual view, which marks changed parts of each page in red.
Press Download diff report to save an HTML report with the word diff, the per-page visual results and both line lists.

content.use: Compare PDF checks two versions of a document and shows you what changed, word by word, so you can spot the difference between a draft and a final copy. A teacher compares a draft and a final handout to see which questions changed. An office worker compares last month's report with this month's to find new figures. A student compares two copies of an assignment to find missing paragraphs. Added words are shown in green and removed words in red, the lines that appear in only one file are listed, and a visual view marks the changed parts of each page in red. You can also download a diff report to keep.
content.tip: Compare the same kind of file with the same kind of file, such as two versions of one report. If the PDFs are scans with no text layer, the tool finds no text to compare, so use OCR PDF on them first.
content.limit: The tool reads the text layer of both PDFs, so scanned-image PDFs give no text to compare — run OCR PDF on them first. The visual view compares the first 10 pages at half size, and pages of different sizes are not pixel-compared. Lines that moved to a different place but stayed the same are not listed as changed.
content.example: Comparing a 10-page draft with the final version shows 12 words added and 5 removed in green and red, 3 lines only in the first PDF and 5 only in the second, and the first changed page marked in red.
faq: Does Compare PDF show me the changed words inside a line?
Yes. Added words are shown in green and removed words in red, inside the changed line. The two lists below still show whole lines that appear in only one file.
Why does it say no text was found?
One or both PDFs are probably scans with no text layer. Run OCR PDF on the scanned file first, then compare the new text PDF.
Can I download the comparison?
Yes. Press Download diff report to save an HTML file with the word diff, the per-page visual results and both line lists.
What does the visual view show?
It renders both PDFs page by page and marks the pixels that differ in red, so you can see where a page changed even when the words look alike. It covers the first 10 pages.

short.en: Extracted text as Markdown.

tools.meta_description: Convert PDF text into Markdown notes with headings, tables and images, free in your browser. Handy for notes and for working with AI tools.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Leave 'Include embedded images' ticked if you want the pictures, or untick it for a single .md file.
Press Convert to Markdown and save the download — a .md file, or a ZIP with document.md and the images.
Open the .md file in your notes app and tidy the headings before you publish it.

content.use: PDF to Markdown turns the text of a PDF into a Markdown file, so you can paste it into notes apps, wikis and editors that use Markdown. A student turns a chapter into Markdown to keep in a notes app. A developer turns a manual into Markdown to put in a project wiki. A writer turns a report into Markdown to edit it in a plain-text editor. Big text becomes headings, bold and italic text keep their marks, lists stay as lists, and tables become Markdown tables. Embedded images are linked in the text and downloaded with the file in a ZIP, so the Markdown keeps its pictures.
content.tip: Open the .md file in your notes app and tidy the headings before you publish it. If you do not need the pictures, untick 'Include embedded images' to download a single .md file instead of a ZIP.
content.limit: Only the text layer is converted. Scanned-image PDFs give no text, so run OCR PDF first. The first row of each table is treated as the header row, and a table with no clear rows and columns becomes plain lines. Fonts and colours are not kept, and a page with mixed columns may read in the wrong order.
content.example: Converting a 6-page manual downloads a ZIP with document.md and two image files, with the price table as a Markdown table and the pictures linked by their file names, such as image-1-1.png and image-3-1.png.
faq: What is Markdown?
Markdown is plain text with simple marks for headings, lists and links. Notes apps, wikis and code editors read it and turn it into formatted text.
Will my tables come through?
Yes, if the text has clear rows and columns. Tables become Markdown tables, with the first row as the header. A table with no clear shape becomes plain lines of text.
What happens to the images in my PDF?
Embedded images are saved as image-1.png, image-2.png and so on, linked in the Markdown, and downloaded with it in a ZIP. Untick 'Include embedded images' to get a single .md file instead.
Can I convert a scanned PDF to Markdown?
Not directly. A scanned PDF has no text layer to read. Use OCR PDF first to make a searchable PDF, then convert that file to Markdown.

short.en: Camera photo or image to PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn camera photos into one PDF, free in your browser. Multi-photo batch, auto-crop and deskew, optional searchable OCR text layer.
steps: Choose one photo or several with the file button, or take photos with your device camera. They go into the PDF in the order you picked them.
Leave the fix-up box ticked to straighten a small tilt and trim the page edges.
Tick 'Add an OCR text layer' and pick a language if you want the PDF to be searchable.
Press Make PDF From Photo and wait — a batch with OCR takes a while, and Cancel stops it after the current photo.
Save the downloaded PDF with your photos as pages.

content.use: Scan to PDF turns photos of pages into one PDF file, which is the quick way to share paper documents from your phone. A student photographs a handwritten assignment and sends it as a PDF. A shop owner photographs receipts and keeps them as one PDF record. An office worker photographs a signed form and emails it as a PDF. Pick one photo or a whole batch: each photo becomes one page of the same PDF, in the order you picked them. The fix-up box straightens a small tilt and trims the page edges, and the OCR box adds a hidden text layer so the PDF is searchable. Nothing is uploaded.
content.tip: Photograph each page straight on, in good light, with the whole page in the frame. A straight, well-lit photo gives a much clearer PDF than a tilted or shadowed one, and the fix-up works best on a plain background.
content.limit: Photos are saved as pictures inside the PDF, so the text is only searchable when you tick the OCR box. The fix-up only corrects a small tilt and trims plain edges; a photo taken at a sharp angle or with heavy shadow may still look tilted. Handwriting is not recognised reliably, and HEIC photos from iPhones are not supported in the browser.
content.example: Photographing four pages of a form and pressing Make PDF From Photo downloads ak-premium-scan.pdf with all four photos as pages, each straightened and trimmed, and with an OCR text layer when the box is ticked.
faq: Can I scan several pages at once?
Yes. Pick several photos in one go and each one becomes a page of the same PDF, in the order you picked them. You no longer need to merge separate PDFs afterwards.
Is the text in my photo searchable?
Only when you tick 'Add an OCR text layer'. The photo is stored as a picture, and the OCR words sit invisibly on top so the PDF can be searched. Handwriting is not recognised reliably.
What does the fix-up do?
It trims the photo to the page edges and straightens a small tilt, up to about 6 degrees. A photo taken at a sharp angle or with heavy shadow may still look tilted.
Can I use the camera directly?
Yes. The file button lets you take a photo with your device camera or pick one from your gallery, depending on your phone or browser.

short.en: Read scanned pages and save them as a text PDF.

tools.meta_description: Read scanned PDF pages as text and save a searchable PDF, free in your browser. Urdu, Arabic, Hindi and English, with auto language detection.
steps: Choose a scanned PDF file with the file button.
Pick a language — English, Urdu, Arabic, Hindi, English + Urdu or English + Arabic — or Auto to detect the script.
Press OCR PDF and wait. The first run downloads the language data, and large files take time.
Save the downloaded searchable PDF when the status says it is done.

content.use: OCR PDF reads the words printed on scanned pages and builds a searchable PDF from them, so a scan you could only look at becomes a file you can search and copy from. A student turns scanned textbook pages into searchable text. An office worker turns a scanned contract into text that can be copied. A researcher turns old scanned papers into text for searching. Each page is kept as a picture of the original, with the recognised words sitting invisibly on top as a text layer. English, Urdu, Arabic and Hindi are available, and Auto detects the script on the first page. The first run downloads the language data, so it takes longer the first time.
content.tip: Use clear, straight scans for the best result. OCR works well on clean printed text and badly on handwriting, faint print or tilted pages. Run it on one page and check the result before you OCR a very long file.
content.limit: OCR reads printed text only. Handwriting, low-quality photos and tilted pages give poor results. Auto detection reads the script, not the language: Urdu and Arabic share a script, so pick Urdu or Arabic yourself when it matters. Large PDFs take a long time because each page is read one by one, and the new PDF holds page pictures with a hidden text layer, not typed text.
content.example: Running OCR PDF on a 3-page scanned Urdu letter with Urdu picked downloads a searchable PDF where each page looks the same as the scan, but the words can be found with search.
faq: Why does the first run take so long?
The tool downloads the OCR language data the first time you use it. Later runs are faster because the data is already there.
Can OCR read handwriting?
Not reliably. OCR is built for clear printed text. Handwriting, faint print and tilted pages give poor or wrong results.
Does OCR keep the look of my scanned page?
Yes. Each page is kept as a picture of the original, with the recognised words sitting invisibly on top as a text layer, so the page looks the same and the words can be searched and copied.
Can OCR read Urdu or other languages?
Yes. Pick Urdu, Arabic or Hindi from the language list, or Auto to detect the script. Urdu and Arabic share a script, so Auto may pick either one — choose the language yourself when it matters.

short.en: Make a fillable form PDF.

tools.meta_description: Make a fillable form PDF with text fields and checkboxes, free in your browser. No sign-up needed.
steps: Type a form title, then add fields one by one: pick a type, type a label, add options for radio or dropdown fields, and pick a check.
Press Create Fillable PDF to download the form, or leave the builder empty for the standard name, email, agree and category form.
To fill a form, choose a fillable PDF, press List Fields, fill in the values and press Download Filled PDF.

content.use: PDF Forms builds a fillable PDF form you can share, or fills in a form you already have. A teacher builds an application form with a name field, an email field and a class dropdown. A shop owner builds a feedback form with a rating dropdown and a comments box. An office worker fills in a form from head office and downloads the filled copy. You can add text, checkbox, radio, dropdown and date fields, mark fields required, and add email or number checks. Required fields are marked with a red star in the PDF. Everything runs in your browser.
content.tip: Add fields in the order you want them to appear, because the form is laid out top to bottom in that order. Test the downloaded form in your own PDF reader before you share it, and check that required fields really block an empty submit there.
content.limit: Forms are built with standard PDF form fields, so they need a reader that supports fillable forms. Email and number rules are written next to the field and checked by this tool when you fill a form here; a PDF reader itself cannot check them. Very long forms flow onto extra pages automatically.
content.example: Adding a Full name text field marked Required, an Email field with the email check, and a Category dropdown, then pressing Create Fillable PDF, downloads a one-page form with those three fields.
faq: What field types can I add?
Text, checkbox, radio (one choice from a list), dropdown and date. Radio and dropdown fields need at least two options, typed as a comma-separated list.
How do the email and number checks work?

When you build a form, the rule is written next to the field and required fields are marked with a red star. When you fill a form with this tool, it checks each value before saving and lists any field that fails.
Can I fill in a PDF form I already have?
Yes. Choose the PDF, press List Fields, fill in each field shown, pick a check per field if you want one, and press Download Filled PDF. Fields the tool does not recognise are skipped.
What happens if I add no fields?
You get the standard one-page form with a name field, an email field, an Agree checkbox and a Category dropdown, under the title you typed.

short.en: Key sentences, in your browser.

tools.meta_description: Summarize a PDF in your browser with key sentences picked locally. No file is sent to an external AI service.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Move the Sentences slider to set how many key sentences you want, and pick Key points or Paragraph style.
Press Summarize PDF, read the summary, and press Download Summary (.txt) to keep it.

content.use: Local Summarizer picks the most important sentences from a PDF and shows them as a short summary, so you can grasp a long document in a minute. A student reads the key sentences of a chapter before an exam. An office worker skims a long report to find what matters. A researcher checks whether a paper is worth reading in full. The tool scores sentences with TF-IDF, which favours words that matter in this document, gives earlier sentences a small boost, and drops near-duplicates. No AI server is used, and the text never leaves your browser.
content.tip: Start with 5 sentences for a quick overview, and raise the slider to 10 for a longer document. Use Key points to scan quickly, or Paragraph to read the summary as flowing text. The summary is a guide; open the full PDF for the details.
content.limit: The summary is extractive: it picks sentences from your document, it does not rewrite them in its own words. It only uses sentences longer than 30 characters, and it works on PDFs with a text layer only; scanned PDFs give no text to summarise. Very short documents may give fewer sentences than the slider asks for.
content.example: Summarising a 20-page report with the slider at 5 in Key points style shows the 5 most important sentences as bullets, with near-duplicates removed.
faq: Is this an AI summary?
No. No AI server is used. The tool scores sentences with TF-IDF, which counts how distinctive each word is in this document, and picks the highest-scoring sentences, all in your browser.
What is the difference between Key points and Paragraph?
Key points shows the top sentences as a bullet list in order of importance. Paragraph shows the same sentences in the order they appear in the document, joined as one paragraph.
Why did I get fewer sentences than I asked for?
Near-duplicate sentences are dropped, and very short documents may not have enough long sentences. The tool shows what it found rather than repeating the same sentence twice.
Can I download the summary?
Yes. After the summary appears, press Download Summary (.txt) to save it as ak-premium-summary.txt.

short.en: Extract text ready to translate.

tools.meta_description: Extract PDF text ready to translate, free in your browser. It prepares the text; translation itself happens elsewhere.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Pick English to Urdu or Urdu to English, then press Find Glossary Terms.
Read the matched terms in the table, or press Download Extracted Text (.txt) to translate the full text elsewhere.

content.use: Translate Helper matches common document words in a PDF against a fixed glossary of 77 English-Urdu terms, in your browser. A student checks the Urdu words for invoice, total, date and payment in a bill. An office worker checks the English words for a Urdu notice. A shop owner looks up the Urdu for discount, tax and balance on a receipt. The matched terms appear in a table in the order they appear in the document. You can also download the full extracted text to translate elsewhere. No text is sent to a translation service.
content.tip: The glossary covers everyday document words such as invoice, bill, receipt, total, tax, amount, customer and delivery. For words outside the list, download the extracted text and translate it in a service you trust.
content.limit: This is glossary matching only, not full translation. Sentences, grammar and words outside the 77-term list are left as they are, and the tool cannot re-lay the translated text into a new PDF. It only reads PDFs with a text layer; scanned PDFs give no text.
content.example: Running Find Glossary Terms on a 1-page bill finds invoice, total, payment and due, and shows each with its Urdu translation in a table.
faq: Does this tool translate my whole PDF?
No. It matches common document words against a fixed glossary of 77 English-Urdu terms and shows the ones found. For a full translation, download the extracted text and use a translation service.
Which words are in the glossary?

Everyday document words: invoice, bill, receipt, total, subtotal, discount, tax, amount, price, quantity, date, name, address, phone, email, customer, order, delivery, payment, balance, signature and similar.
Can I translate from Urdu to English?
Yes. Pick Urdu to English in the Direction list and the tool finds Urdu glossary words in the PDF and shows their English meanings.
Can I use it on a scanned PDF?
No. A scanned PDF has no text layer, so the tool finds nothing to match. Use OCR PDF first to make a text PDF, then run Translate Helper on the new file.

short.en: Real tables into an .xlsx file, with merged cells.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Find Tables. If the PDF is a scan, tick the OCR option first — it reads the page as text so tables can be found.
Tick the tables you want, press Download Excel, and check a few cells before trusting a total.

content.use: Converting a PDF to Excel is for getting numbers out of a PDF table: a bank statement, a price list, a stock report or a fee table that needs to be sorted, totalled or charted. Once the numbers are in a spreadsheet they are real Excel values, so you can total them, sort them and chart them. Empty cells keep their column position, so a Total row with empty quantity and price cells still puts its total in the Total column.
content.tip: Tables with clear gaps between columns convert best. If a table has merged cells, the merged value spans the right number of columns in Excel. Use Find Tables first and tick only the tables you need — each one gets its own sheet. After downloading, check a total row before you trust it.
content.limit: Tables are detected from the positions of words on the page. A table with no gaps between columns, rotated text or a complicated layout may not split cleanly, so check a few cells before you trust a total. Scanned PDFs need the OCR option, which reads English text only and is slower.
content.example: A price list PDF with item, quantity, price and total columns becomes a spreadsheet with those four columns, the prices stored as numbers so you can total them in Excel. A Total row at the bottom with empty quantity and price cells still exports its total in the Total column, not shifted left.
faq: Do empty cells keep their column in the spreadsheet?
Yes. An empty cell is kept as an empty cell in its own column, so a Total row with empty quantity and price cells still puts its total in the Total column, not shifted left into an earlier column.
Are the numbers in my Excel file real numbers?
Yes. Prices, quantities and totals are stored as real Excel numbers, and dates and currency are stored with their Excel types, so you can total, sort and chart them.
What happens with merged cells?
A cell that spans several columns in the PDF is written as a merged range in Excel, so the value appears once and covers the same columns it covered in the PDF.
What if my PDF has several tables?
Each table you tick gets its own sheet in the downloaded file, named Table 1, Table 2, and so on, in the order they appear in the PDF.

tools.meta_description: Convert PDF tables to Excel, free in your browser. Numbers, dates and currency become real Excel values, with merged cells and one sheet per table.

short.en: Headings, tables and images into a .docx file.

steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
If the PDF is a scan with no text, tick the OCR option before converting.
Press Convert PDF to Word and save the downloaded .docx file.
Headings in the Word file use the Heading 1, 2 and 3 styles, so the document outline in Word lists the structure.

content.use: PDF to Word is for editing a document that only exists as a PDF: a letter, a report or a form that needs changes. The tool reads the font sizes in the PDF, so large lines become real Word heading styles, bold and italic text is kept, and tables are rebuilt as real Word tables with a bold header row. Pictures from the PDF are placed in the document in the right order. The Word file can then be edited, spell-checked and printed like any other document, and it opens in Word, Google Docs and other word processors. The conversion runs in your browser, so the file is never uploaded.
content.tip: Check the Word file after the conversion, because a table with no clear grid or a heading that is the same size as the body text will come out as plain paragraphs. For a scanned PDF, tick the OCR option first, otherwise the tool finds no text.
content.limit: The conversion rebuilds the document from the text in the PDF, so it is not a pixel-perfect copy. Original fonts, exact spacing, multi-column layouts, charts and complex tables are not preserved. A scanned PDF with no text layer needs the OCR option, and handwriting or blurry scans give poor results.
content.example: A 2-page letter with a bold heading, a price table and a logo becomes a Word file with a real heading, a real table and the logo in place, ready to edit.
faq: Does the Word file keep my headings as real headings?

Yes. Lines that are clearly larger than the body text become Word heading styles, so you can use Word's navigation pane and build a table of contents from them. Lines the same size as the body text stay as normal paragraphs.
Are tables in the PDF rebuilt as Word tables?

Yes, when the table has a clear grid of rows and columns. The first row becomes a bold header row, and merged cells are kept as merged cells. Tables without clear lines or spacing may come out as plain paragraphs instead.
Do pictures from the PDF appear in the Word file?
Yes. Pictures are taken from the PDF in their original form and placed in the document in the same order as the pages and paragraphs around them, scaled to fit the page width.
What if my PDF has no text at all?
Tick the OCR option before converting. The tool reads the scanned pages with text recognition first, then builds the Word file from that text. Handwriting and blurry scans give poor results.

tools.meta_description: Turn a PDF into an editable Word document with real headings, tables and images, free in your browser. No upload.

short.en: Each PDF page as a widescreen slide with tables and images.

tools.meta_description: Turn each PDF page into a PowerPoint slide with titles, bullets, tables and images, free in your browser. No upload.
steps: Choose a PDF file with the file button.
Press Convert PDF to PPT.
Save the downloaded .pptx file, which has one widescreen slide per PDF page.
