Text that does not fit on a slide is kept in the speaker notes, and tables and pictures from the PDF are placed on the slide.

content.use: PDF to PPT turns each page of a PDF into a slide in a PowerPoint file, so you can present or edit the words from a document. A student turns a report into slides for a class presentation. An office worker turns a briefing into slides for a meeting. The largest line on each page becomes the slide title in large bold text, indented lines become real bullet points, and tables and pictures from the page are placed on the slide. Text that does not fit the slide is moved to the speaker notes, so nothing is lost. The file downloads as a .pptx that opens in PowerPoint and other slide apps.
content.tip: Check the slides after the conversion and tidy the titles, because the largest line on a page is not always a real heading. Text that did not fit is in the speaker notes, so open the notes pane to find it.
content.limit: The conversion is a text reconstruction, not a pixel-perfect copy. Fonts, colours, exact positions and animations are not preserved. Each PDF page becomes one widescreen slide, and a scanned PDF with no text layer cannot be converted, so run OCR PDF first to add text.
content.example: Converting a 5-page briefing downloads ak-premium-pdf-to-ppt.pptx with 5 widescreen slides, each with a title, bullet points and the tables and pictures from its page.
faq: How does the tool choose the slide title?
It takes the largest line of text on each page and makes it the slide title in large bold text. If no line is clearly larger than the rest, the first line becomes the title.
What happens to text that does not fit on a slide?
It is moved to the speaker notes for that slide, so nothing is lost. Open the notes pane in PowerPoint or Google Slides to read it and decide what to keep.
Do tables and pictures come across?
Yes. Tables with a clear grid become real PowerPoint tables, and pictures from the page are placed on the slide. Pictures that would cover the text are moved to the bottom of the slide instead.
What if my PDF is a scan?
The tool will say no readable text was found. Run OCR PDF first to make a text PDF, then convert that file to PPT.

short.en: Paste text or Markdown, download a styled PDF.

tools.meta_description: Paste text or Markdown and download a PDF with headings, tables, headers and page numbers, free in your browser. No upload.
steps: Paste your text into the box and choose Plain text or Markdown.
Type a header or footer if you want one, and keep page numbers ticked to number the pages.
Press Convert Text to PDF and save the downloaded PDF.
For Markdown, use # for a main heading, - for list items, and | pipes | for a table, then convert.

content.use: TXT / HTML to PDF turns pasted text into a PDF file, which is handy when you have words in a message, a note or a web page and need them as a document. A student pastes an essay draft and downloads it as a PDF to submit. An office worker pastes a notice from an email and saves it as a PDF. A shop owner pastes a price list from a chat and sends it as a PDF. Choose Markdown to keep headings, bold and italic text, lists and tables, or plain text for simple words. You can add a header, a footer and page numbers to every page. Nothing is uploaded; the PDF is built in your browser.
content.tip: Write Markdown with # for a heading, - for a bullet list and | for a table, then check the PDF, because very long tables and code blocks flow across pages.
content.limit: Markdown tables and code blocks are kept, but HTML tags in the pasted text are not rendered, and you cannot choose the font or page size. Very long text flows across pages automatically, with the header and footer on every page.
content.example: Pasting # Price List with a small Markdown table and pressing Convert Text to PDF downloads ak-premium-text-to-pdf.pdf with a heading, the table and page numbers.
faq: What Markdown can I use?
Headings with #, bold with **, italic with *, bullet lists with -, numbered lists, tables with |, code blocks with ``` and quotes with >. Anything else is treated as plain text.
Can I add a header and page numbers?
Yes. Type the header and footer text in the boxes and they appear on every page. Keep page numbers ticked to add Page 1 of 3 at the bottom of each page.
Does the tool keep my HTML formatting?
No. HTML tags in the pasted text are not rendered. Use Markdown mode for headings, bold, lists and tables, or plain text mode for simple words.
Is my pasted text uploaded anywhere?
No. The PDF is built in your browser with jsPDF, so nothing is sent to a server. The text never leaves your device, and closing the tab removes it from the page.

short.en: Every sheet as a styled PDF with tables and charts.

content.use: Excel to PDF is for sharing a sheet that must not be changed: a price list, a report or a table for a client. Every sheet in the file becomes pages in the PDF, each with its own sheet-name heading, so nothing is left behind. The cells are drawn as a real table with column widths, cell colours, bold text and number formats kept, and the table header repeats on every page. You can add a bar or line chart drawn from the first numeric column, and choose portrait or landscape with fit-to-page scaling for wide tables. The PDF shows the values, not the formulas, and it opens on any phone or computer.
content.tip: Use landscape and fit to the page width for wide tables, and keep the first numeric column as the one you want charted. Check that the chart matches the numbers before you share the PDF.
content.limit: The PDF shows cell values, not formulas, and charts are drawn from the first numeric column only. Very wide tables are scaled down when fit to the page is on, which can make small text hard to read. Exact Excel fonts and print settings are not preserved.
content.example: A workbook with a Sales sheet and a Stock sheet becomes a PDF with a heading and a table for each sheet, plus a bar chart of the sales figures.
faq: Are all sheets in my workbook converted?
Yes. Every sheet with data becomes pages in the PDF, each starting with its own sheet-name heading. Empty sheets are skipped.
Does the PDF keep my cell colours and bold text?
Yes. Cell colours, bold text and number formats are carried into the PDF table, and the header row repeats at the top of every page the table spans.
How does the chart work?

Pick a bar or line chart and the tool draws it from the first column where most of the values are numbers, using the first column as the labels. If no numeric column is found, no chart is added and the tool says so.
Are the formulas in my Excel file kept?
No. The PDF shows the values, not the formulas, so the numbers are what you see in the sheet. If you change a value in Excel, convert the file again to update the PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn every Excel sheet into a styled PDF with tables, colours and charts, free in your browser. No upload.
steps: Choose an Excel (.xlsx or .xls) file with the file button.
Pick portrait or landscape, and tick Fit to the page width if the table is wide.
Choose a bar or line chart if you want one from the first numeric column, then press Convert Excel to PDF.
Pick Landscape in the Orientation list for wide tables, and keep Fit wide tables to the page width ticked so nothing is cut off.

short.en: Word document with headings, tables and images as PDF.

content.use: Word to PDF is for sending a document that must look the same everywhere: a CV, a letter or a form. A PDF cannot be edited by mistake, and it opens on any phone or computer. The tool reads the document properly, so headings become large bold headings, lists become bullet or numbered lists, tables become real PDF tables and pictures from the document are placed in the PDF. You can add a header and footer, page numbers, and a table of contents built from the headings. The conversion runs in your browser, so the file is never uploaded, and the PDF is ready to send or print.
content.tip: Use the table of contents only when the document has real headings, because it is built from them. Check the PDF after converting, since exact Word spacing and fonts are not kept.
content.limit: This is a browser rendering, not Word itself. Exact Word fonts, page layout, tracked changes and comments are not preserved, and very complex documents may look different. Only .docx files are accepted.
content.example: A Word letter with a heading, a bullet list and a small table becomes a PDF with the same heading, list and table, plus page numbers at the bottom.
faq: Are images in my Word file kept in the PDF?
Yes. Pictures in the document are placed in the PDF in the same order as the text around them, scaled to fit the page width. Very large pictures are scaled down.
How does the table of contents work?
Tick the option and the tool builds a contents page from the headings in the document, with the page number each heading lands on. It only works when the document uses real heading styles.
Can I add a header and footer?
Yes. Type the header and footer text in the boxes and they appear on every page. Tick page numbers to add Page 1 of 3 at the bottom of each page.
Does it keep tracked changes?
No. Tracked changes and comments are not carried into the PDF. Accept the changes in Word first if you want the final text.

tools.meta_description: Turn a Word document into a PDF with headings, lists, tables and images kept, free in your browser. No upload.
steps: Choose a Word (.docx) file with the file button.
Type a header or footer if you want one, and tick page numbers or the table of contents.
Press Convert Word to PDF and save the downloaded PDF.
If the Word file has tracked changes or comments, accept them in Word first, as they are not shown in the PDF.

short.en: Each slide as a styled PDF page with images.

content.use: PowerPoint to PDF is for sharing slides that must look the same on any device, or for printing a deck without PowerPoint. A PDF is also easier to attach to an email than a large presentation file. The tool reads each slide properly, so text boxes are drawn at their slide positions with their sizes, colours, bold and italic text, and pictures are placed where they are on the slide. Each slide becomes one PDF page at the same size as the deck, so the page count matches the slide count. The conversion runs in your browser, so the file is never uploaded.
content.tip: Check the first page of the PDF after converting, because a text box that runs past the slide edge will run past the page edge too. For the best result, keep the slide text inside the slide.
content.limit: This is a browser rendering, not PowerPoint itself. Slide designs, charts, animations and transitions are not preserved, and text is drawn in a standard font, so the PDF will not look exactly like the slides. Only .pptx files are accepted.
content.example: A 5-slide deck with a title, bullet points and a photo on each slide becomes a 5-page PDF with the text and photos in place.
faq: Is this a full PowerPoint to PDF conversion?
No. It keeps the text boxes at their slide positions with their sizes and colours, and the pictures, but slide designs, charts and animations are not carried over.
What if a slide has no text?
That slide becomes a page that says there is no text on the slide, so the page count still matches the deck.
Can I convert an old .ppt file?
No. The tool only accepts .pptx files. Open the deck in PowerPoint and save it as .pptx first, then convert the new file.
Does each slide become one PDF page?
Yes. Each slide becomes one PDF page at the same size as the deck, so a 5-slide deck becomes a 5-page PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn PowerPoint slides into a PDF with text positions and images kept, free in your browser. No upload.
steps: Choose a PowerPoint (.pptx) file with the file button.
Press Convert PPT to PDF.
Save the downloaded PDF, which has one page per slide.
Open the downloaded PDF to check each slide, as charts and animations from the presentation are not carried over.

short.en: Describe it, get a formula.

steps: Pick the task from the list, for example AVERAGEIF, EOMONTH, RANK, LARGE, ROUND, VLOOKUP with IFERROR, multi-criteria XLOOKUP, or LET.
Fill in the labelled fields with your own ranges and values.
Press Generate, copy the formula and paste it into Excel, then read the validation line. To check any formula, paste it in the Check a formula box and press Check Formula.
Test the formula on a copy of your data first, so a mistake cannot change your real workbook.

content.use: An Excel formula generator is for the spreadsheet jobs that are easy to describe but hard to write from memory: averaging sales for one city, finding the last day of a month, ranking a list, rounding a price, or looking up a price with a blank cell when there is no match. Pick the task, fill in the labelled fields, and the tool builds the exact formula with a plain-language explanation and an example. Every generated formula is checked before it is shown: brackets must balance, every function name must be a real Excel function, and a formula parser runs over it when it loads.
content.tip: Fill in the fields with your own ranges and values, then read the validation line under the example. If it says a function is not implemented in the in-browser parser, the formula can still be right: LET, XLOOKUP and RANK are real Excel functions that the parser does not run.
content.limit: The tool builds formulas from fixed templates, not from AI. It does not read your workbook and cannot guess your cell addresses. Validation checks brackets, function names and parser errors; it cannot tell whether your ranges hold the data you expect. Always test a formula on a copy of your data first.
content.example: Choosing VLOOKUP with IFERROR, entering A2 as the value, Sheet2!A:B as the table and 2 as the column gives =IFERROR(VLOOKUP(A2, Sheet2!A:B, 2, FALSE), "") which shows a blank cell instead of #N/A when there is no match.
faq: Does it write formulas by itself?
No. The tool uses fixed, parameterized templates. You pick the task and fill in the fields, and it builds the exact formula from those values. It does not guess or learn from your data.
Why does my formula show an error in Excel?
The most common reason is a range that does not exist in your sheet, or a sheet name that needs quotes. Check the ranges, and test on a copy of your data.
Which formulas can it build?

Twenty. SUMIF, SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX plus MATCH, IF, Nested IF, TEXT, DATEDIF, UNIQUE, AVERAGEIF, EOMONTH, RANK, LARGE, SMALL, ROUND, VLOOKUP with IFERROR, XLOOKUP with several criteria, and LET. Pick one from the Task list.
Does it explain the formula too?
Yes. The result shows the formula, a plain-language explanation of what each part does, and an example you can follow.

tools.meta_description: Generate Excel formulas from a plain-words description, free in your browser. Describe the task, get the formula.

short.en: Paste a formula, understand it.

tools.meta_description: Paste an Excel formula and understand what it does, free in your browser. A plain-words explanation, step by step.
steps: Paste a formula that starts with = in the 'Formula' box, for example =VLOOKUP(A2, Sheet2!A:B, 2, FALSE).
Press Explain Formula.
Read the explanation in the box below, which lists each function found and what it does.

content.use: Formula Explainer reads an Excel formula and explains it in plain words, so you can understand a formula someone else wrote or check your own work. A student pastes a VLOOKUP from a class example to learn what each part does. An office worker pastes a SUMIF from a shared report to see why the total looks wrong. A shop owner pastes an IF formula from a price sheet to understand the condition. The tool lists the functions it finds and explains each one from its dictionary, then gives a plain-language reading of the whole formula. It does not run the formula or check your numbers; it explains what the formula says.
content.tip: Paste the full formula including the = sign, or the tool will ask you to. If a function is not in the dictionary, the tool says so; check Excel help for that function's exact arguments.
content.limit: The tool explains 8 functions only: SUM, IF, VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX, MATCH, COUNTIF and SUMIF. Any other function gets a note that it is not in the dictionary yet. The tool does not run the formula, check your cell references or test it against your data.
content.example: Pasting =VLOOKUP(A2, Sheet2!A:B, 2, FALSE) explains that VLOOKUP searches the first column of a table and returns a value from a column to its right.
faq: Which functions can the tool explain?
Eight: SUM, IF, VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX, MATCH, COUNTIF and SUMIF. Other functions get a note that they are not in the dictionary yet.
Does the tool run my formula?
No. It reads the formula and explains what each part does. It does not open your workbook or check whether the result is correct.
Why does it say my formula must start with =?
Excel formulas start with an equals sign. Paste the whole formula, including the =, or the tool cannot read it.
Can I use the explanation in my work?
Yes. The explanation is plain text you can read and learn from. Always test the formula on a copy of your data before you use it in a real sheet.

short.en: Describe it, get VBA code.

content.use: A VBA macro writer is for repeating a job in Excel without doing it by hand every time: marking rows that meet a condition, copying filtered rows to a report sheet, importing a CSV file, building a PivotTable, emailing a report with its file attached, protecting sheets, adding a dropdown list, replacing text across the whole workbook, or splitting and merging workbooks. Pick the task, fill in the labelled fields, and the tool builds the macro from a fixed template. A syntax checker is built in: paste any VBA code and it checks that Sub, If, For, With and Select blocks are closed and that quotes and brackets balance.
content.tip: Start with a small task, such as looping through rows, and test the macro on a copy of your workbook. Press Alt + F11 in Excel, insert a module, paste the code, and run it from there. Change the placeholder paths and passwords before you run a template.
content.limit: The tool builds macros from fixed templates. It does not write a macro for a job it has no template for, and it cannot test the macro against your workbook. The syntax check is a static check only: it cannot tell whether a sheet, range or Outlook reference exists. Macros only run in Excel for Windows or Mac with macros enabled.
content.example: Choosing Import a CSV file, with sheet Data and the path C:\Reports\sales.csv, gives a macro that clears the sheet and imports the file, splitting values at commas.
faq: How do I run the macro in Excel?
Press Alt + F11, insert a module, paste the code, close the editor, then press Alt + F8 and run the macro. Save the file as .xlsm if you want to keep the macro.
Is the macro safe to run?
Read it first. It only does what the template says: it works on the sheet and range you entered. Test it on a copy of your workbook before you run it on real data.
Which macros can it write?

Fifteen. Loop through rows, copy data, AutoFilter, sort, hide a sheet, copy filtered rows, import CSV, PivotTable, Outlook mail with attachment, protect and unprotect sheets, dropdown list, find and replace, split workbook, and merge workbooks.
Can I check my own VBA code?

Yes. Paste it in the Check my VBA code box and press Check Syntax. The tool checks that every Sub, If, For, With and Select block is closed and that quotes and brackets balance. It cannot tell whether a sheet or range exists.

tools.meta_description: Write Excel VBA macros from a plain-words description, free in your browser. Describe the automation, get VBA code.
steps: Pick a task in the 'Task' list: Loop through rows, Copy data to another sheet, AutoFilter a table, Sort a table, Hide a sheet, Copy filtered rows, Import CSV, PivotTable, Outlook mail with attachment, Protect or Unprotect sheets, Dropdown list, Find and replace, Split workbook, or Merge workbooks.
Fill in the labelled fields that appear for that task.
Press Generate and copy the VBA code from the box below. To check code you wrote yourself, paste it in the Check my VBA code box and press Check Syntax.
In Excel press Alt + F11, paste the code into a module, and press F5 to run it on a copy of your workbook.

short.en: Build patterns, extract emails.

content.use: A regex creator is for finding or checking a pattern in text: an email address, a Pakistan mobile number, a CNIC, an NTN, a Pakistan IBAN, a passport number, a postal code, an amount with commas, a time, Urdu text, a date, or a web link. It is used in spreadsheets, text editors and data cleaning, where a pattern is faster than reading every line. Pick a pattern, test it on your own text with matches highlighted and capture groups listed, or build one from blocks. An explain mode reads any pattern token by token and says what each part means in plain words.
content.tip: Paste some of your own text in the test box and press Generate. The tool highlights every match in your text and lists the capture groups, so you can see if the pattern is right before you use it anywhere else.
content.limit: The tool gives you a fixed pattern for a named task. It does not build a pattern for a new, unusual format, and a pattern that matches your test text may still miss a different format of the same thing. The explain mode describes tokens; it does not run the pattern.
content.example: Choosing Pakistan mobile number gives a pattern that finds 0300-1234567. Choosing Pakistan IBAN gives \bPK\d{2}[A-Z]{4}\d{16}\b, which finds PK36SCBL0000001123456702. Choosing Urdu text gives a pattern that finds اردو in mixed English and Urdu text.
faq: What is a regex?
A regular expression is a short pattern that describes a shape of text, such as an email address. A program can then find every piece of text with that shape.
Can I use this pattern in Excel?
Yes, with VBA, or in Google Sheets with REGEXEXTRACT. Paste the pattern exactly as shown, including the backslashes, and test it on a small range first.
Which patterns can it create?

Thirteen. Email address, Pakistan mobile number, date in DD/MM/YYYY form, web link, numbers in text, Pakistan CNIC, NTN, Pakistan IBAN, passport, postal code, amount with commas, time, and Urdu text. Pick one from the Pattern list.
Can I test the pattern on my own text?
Yes. Paste text in the test box and press Generate. Matches are highlighted in your text, and capture groups are listed below, so you can check the pattern before you use it.

tools.meta_description: Build regex patterns and extract emails and dates, free in your browser. Describe the pattern, get working regex.
steps: Pick a pattern in the 'Pattern for' list: Email address, Pakistan mobile number, Date (DD/MM/YYYY), Web link, Numbers in text, Pakistan CNIC, NTN, Pakistan IBAN, Passport, Postal code, Amount with commas, Time, or Urdu text.
Paste some text in the 'Test text' box if you want to test the pattern. Matches are highlighted in your text, and capture groups are listed below.

Press Generate Pattern and copy the pattern from the box below. To build a pattern of your own, add blocks in the builder and press Test Built Pattern. To understand a pattern, paste it in the explain box.
Copy the pattern into your own tool or code, and test it again there with your real data before you rely on it.

short.en: Describe it, get a DAX measure.

content.use: A DAX measure is for Power BI and Excel Power Pivot: a total, an average, a year-to-date figure, a share of the total, a month-on-month or year-on-year change, a running total, a moving average, a rank, a top N total, or one measure that changes with a slicer. It is the calculation behind most Power BI cards and charts. Pick the measure, fill in your table and column names, and the tool builds it from a fixed template with an explanation. A syntax checker is built in: paste any measure and it checks brackets, quotes and bracket references.
content.tip: Use your real table and column names in the fields. The measure name is the name that will appear in your report, so make it clear, such as Total Sales. Time measures need a date table: the Date Table task builds one for you.
content.limit: The tool builds measures from fixed templates. It does not connect to your Power BI file and cannot check that your table or column names are right. The syntax check cannot tell whether a table or column exists in your model. Paste the measure into Power BI and test it there.
content.example: Choosing Month on Month growth, with measure Total Sales and date 'Calendar'[Date], gives a measure that compares this month with last month as a percentage.
faq: What is DAX?
DAX is the formula language of Power BI and Excel Power Pivot. A measure is a calculation, such as a total, that is worked out when a user looks at the report.
Why does my measure show an error in Power BI?
The table or column name is usually the reason. Check the spelling and the square brackets, and make sure the table exists in your model.
Which measures can it build?

Sixteen. Total Sales, Average, Year to Date, Percent of Total, Count Rows, Month on Month growth, Year on Year growth, Running Total, Moving Average, Previous Month, Month to Date, Quarter to Date, RANKX, Top N total, SWITCH dynamic measure, and a Date Table.
Can I check my own DAX measure?

Yes. Paste it in the Check my DAX measure box and press Check Syntax. The tool checks brackets, quotes and square brackets, and warns about function names it does not recognise. It cannot check your table or column names.

tools.meta_description: Write DAX measures for Power BI from a plain-words description, free in your browser. Describe the measure, get DAX.
steps: Pick a measure in the 'Task' list: Total Sales, Average, Year to Date, Percent of Total, Count Rows, Month on Month growth, Year on Year growth, Running Total, Moving Average, Previous Month, Month to Date, Quarter to Date, RANKX, Top N total, SWITCH dynamic measure, or Date Table.
Fill in the labelled fields with your table and column names.
Press Generate, then copy the DAX measure and paste it into Power BI or Excel Power Pivot. To check a measure you wrote yourself, paste it in the Check my DAX measure box and press Check Syntax.
Test the measure in Power BI on a copy of your model first, and check its total against a number you already trust.

short.en: First sheet exported as CSV.

tools.meta_description: Export the first sheet of an Excel file as CSV, free in your browser. Your file never leaves your device.
steps: Choose an Excel file (.xlsx or .xls) with the file button. The sheet list fills in from your file.
Pick the sheet, the export scope, the delimiter, and the options: UTF-8 BOM, visible rows only, and skip empty rows.
Press Convert Excel to CSV. One sheet downloads as a .csv file; all sheets download as one ZIP file with a CSV per sheet.
Open the downloaded CSV in a text editor or Excel to check the delimiter and the rows before you send it on.

content.use: Excel to CSV exports a sheet of an Excel workbook as a plain .csv file, so the data can be opened in other apps or uploaded to a system that only takes CSV. A shop owner exports a stock list to upload to an online store. An office worker exports a customer list to import into another program. A student exports a class list to use in a different app. Pick any sheet, or export every sheet at once as a ZIP. Choose the delimiter, add a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens Urdu and special characters correctly, skip hidden rows, and skip empty rows. Values are saved as they appear in Excel, with dates and numbers formatted.
content.tip: Check the sheet list after choosing your file: the first sheet is selected by default. Open the .csv afterwards to check that dates and numbers look right, and that Urdu text opens correctly.
content.limit: Formulas are saved as their calculated values, and formatting, colours, charts and other sheets are not kept in a single-sheet export. An empty sheet gives an error and nothing is downloaded. Hidden rows are only skipped when the visible-rows-only box is ticked.
content.example: Converting a workbook with a Sales sheet and a Stock sheet, with all sheets selected, downloads ak-premium-excel-to-csv.zip holding Sales.csv and Stock.csv.
faq: Which sheet is exported?
The sheet you pick in the Sheet list. The first sheet is selected by default. Choose All sheets in the Export list to get every sheet at once, one CSV per sheet in a ZIP file.
Does the CSV keep my formulas?
No. Formulas are saved as their calculated values. The .csv file holds plain values separated by commas, with no formatting.
What happens if the sheet is empty?
The tool shows a message that the selected sheet is empty and downloads nothing. Pick a sheet with data, or choose a different workbook.
Can I choose the delimiter?

Yes. Pick comma, semicolon, tab or pipe in the Delimiter list. Comma is the default. Use semicolon if your data already has commas inside the values, or if the system you upload to expects semicolons.

short.en: CSV text saved as .xlsx.

tools.meta_description: Save CSV text as an .xlsx spreadsheet, free in your browser. Paste CSV rows and download Excel instantly.
steps: Choose one or more .csv files with the file button, or paste CSV text in the 'Paste CSV text' box.
Press Preview First Rows to see the first rows, the detected delimiter and the encoding. Pick a different delimiter in the list if the preview looks wrong.
Press Convert CSV to Excel. The first row becomes a bold header with frozen panes and AutoFilter, numbers and dates become real Excel types, and each file becomes its own sheet.
Open the downloaded workbook in Excel and check that the dates and numbers read back with the right types.

content.use: CSV to Excel turns a .csv file or pasted CSV text into an Excel workbook, so it opens in Excel with rows and columns. A shop owner turns a sales CSV into an Excel file to sort and filter it. An office worker turns a system export into Excel to add totals. A student turns survey results into Excel to make a chart. The tool detects the delimiter and the file encoding by itself, shows a preview of the first rows, and turns numbers, dates and true/false values into real Excel types. The header row is bold with frozen panes and AutoFilter, column widths are fitted, and several CSV files become one workbook with a sheet per file.
content.tip: Press Preview First Rows before converting: if the columns look wrong, the delimiter is probably wrong, so pick it in the list. Check that the first row holds your column names, because it becomes the header row.
content.limit: The result holds values only, with no formulas or charts. Dates must be written as YYYY-MM-DD or DD/MM/YYYY to be recognised as dates. A phone number starting with 0 stays as text so the zero is not lost. Very unusual CSV files may still not split correctly, so check the preview first.
content.example: Pasting 'name,age,joined' on the first line and 'Ali,25,2026-01-15' on the second gives an .xlsx file where 25 is a real number, the date is a real date, and the header row is bold with a filter.
faq: Can I paste text instead of a file?
Either works. Choose one or more .csv files, or paste the CSV text into the box. If you upload files, the pasted text is ignored.
What becomes the header row?
The first row of your CSV becomes the header row of the Excel sheet, so put your column names there.
Does the Excel file keep my formatting?
The CSV has no formatting to keep, but the tool adds some: a bold header row, frozen panes, AutoFilter and fitted column widths. Add colours and formulas in Excel afterwards.
What if my CSV uses semicolons?
The tool detects the delimiter by itself, including semicolons, tabs and pipes. Check the preview: if the columns look wrong, pick the delimiter in the list before you convert.

short.en: Batch compress images, ZIP download, AVIF output.

steps: Choose one or more images with the file button.
Tick Fix rotation from photo data if a phone photo comes out sideways.
Pick a format and set the quality with the slider.
Type a target size in KB if the file must fit under a limit.
Press Compress Images and save the result. Several images download as one ZIP file.

content.use: Image Compressor makes JPG, PNG, WebP and AVIF pictures smaller without changing what they show. A shop owner shrinks product photos before uploading them, so the online shop loads faster. A student shrinks a scanned assignment to fit under a portal file size limit. The quality slider trades a little sharpness for a smaller file, and the target size mode lowers the quality step by step until the file fits. Phone photos are turned the right way up from their photo data, and re-saving a photo never keeps its location data. The pictures are compressed in your browser, so your images are never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use a quality of 80 for photos on a website: the file shrinks a lot and the picture still looks sharp. Use WebP when the other side accepts it, because WebP is smaller than JPG at the same quality. AVIF is smaller still, but it only opens in Chrome and Edge. If a photo comes out sideways, tick Fix rotation from photo data and compress it again.
content.limit: Images up to 50 MB each are accepted. AVIF only saves in Chrome and Edge; other browsers show an honest message and suggest WebP instead. Re-saving a photo strips its location data and other photo details, and a very small file may grow instead of shrinking. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Compressing a 2 MB phone photo at quality 80 gives a JPG of about 400 KB that looks the same on screen.
faq: Why did my file get bigger after compressing?

A very small or already compressed file has little left to throw away, so re-saving it can add a little size instead. This is normal. Try a lower quality, or a different format such as WebP, to get a smaller file.
Does compressing remove location data from photos?
Yes. Re-saving a photo strips the location data and other details stored inside the file. This happens whether the rotation box is ticked or not, so a compressed photo is safe to share.
Why is AVIF not offered in my browser?
AVIF only saves in Chrome and Edge. Safari and Firefox cannot save AVIF from a canvas yet. The tool says so honestly and suggests WebP instead, which is almost as small and opens everywhere.
How do I compress several images at once?
Choose more than one image with the file button. Each image gets its own download link and preview, and when there is more than one image they also download together as a single ZIP file.

tools.meta_description: Compress JPG, PNG, WebP and AVIF images in batches in your browser, with a quality slider and a target-size mode. Download one file or a ZIP.

short.en: Resize by width and height.

tools.meta_description: Resize images by width and height in pixels, free in your browser. No upload, no sign-up.
steps: Choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image with the file button. The original size is filled in for you.
Pick a size preset like Instagram post or Passport, or type the Width and Height in pixels yourself. Tick Keep aspect ratio to change the other side automatically.
Tick Face-aware crop when you want the crop centred on a face. It needs Chrome, and it falls back to the centre of the picture when no face is found.
Choose PNG, JPG, WebP or AVIF as the output format, and a quality level for JPG, WebP and AVIF.
Press Resize Image and save the downloaded file, which has the size you chose.

content.use: Image Resizer changes the size of a picture to exactly what you need, in your browser. It has ready presets for Instagram posts and stories, Facebook posts, YouTube thumbnails, LinkedIn posts, WhatsApp display pictures, passport photos and A4 pages at 150 and 300 DPI, so you do not have to look up the numbers. You can also type any width and height, keep the shape with the aspect ratio box, and choose PNG, JPG, WebP or AVIF with a quality level. When a face matters, the face-aware crop keeps the person in the frame instead of cutting them off. Nothing is uploaded, so your picture stays on your device.
content.tip: Use a preset for social media, since each site asks for its own size. For a photo you will print, use the A4 preset at 300 DPI and PNG or JPG at 92 percent quality.
content.limit: Face-aware crop needs the FaceDetector built into Chrome, so other browsers crop from the centre instead. AVIF output needs a browser that can save AVIF. Width and height must stay between 1 and 8000 pixels.
content.example: A 4000 pixel wide photo resized to the Instagram post preset becomes 1080 by 1080 pixels, with the face kept in the middle of the square.
faq: What size is an Instagram post
An Instagram post is 1080 by 1080 pixels, and a story is 1080 by 1920 pixels. Pick Instagram post or Instagram story from the preset list and the numbers are filled in for you.
How does face-aware crop work

When you tick the box, the tool looks for a face in the picture and centres the crop on it, so the person stays in the frame. It needs Chrome, and it crops from the centre when no face is found or the browser cannot do it.
Will resizing make my photo blurry

Making a picture smaller keeps it sharp, and making it bigger softens it, because no new detail can be added. Start from the largest original you have, and do not enlarge a small picture more than you need to.
Which format is smallest
WebP is usually the smallest for the same quality, followed by JPG, while PNG is the largest. Use WebP for the web, JPG for photos you share, and PNG when you need transparency or sharp text.

short.en: Change JPG, PNG, WebP format.

tools.meta_description: Change image format between JPG, PNG and WebP, free in your browser. Convert images without uploading them.
steps: Choose one or more JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, BMP, GIF, ICO or TIFF images with the file button. Tick Batch mode to convert several at once.
Pick the output format: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, BMP, GIF or ICO. For JPG, WebP and AVIF, choose a quality level too.
Leave Auto-rotate on to fix phone photos that were saved sideways. For JPG output, tick Keep EXIF to carry the photo details across.
Press Convert Image and wait for the progress message to finish.
Save the downloaded file, or the ZIP when you converted several images at once. TIFF input works, and GIF output is a still image.

content.use: Image Converter changes the format of your pictures without uploading them anywhere. It accepts JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, BMP, GIF, ICO and TIFF files, and it can turn several images into JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, BMP, GIF or ICO at once. Phone photos that were saved sideways are fixed automatically from their EXIF orientation, and JPG output can keep the original photo details when you tick the box. TIFF files are decoded in your browser, BMP and GIF are written byte by byte because browsers cannot save those formats, and ICO files hold 16, 32 and 48 pixel sizes for app and website icons. Everything runs on your own device, so your pictures never leave your computer.
content.tip: For the smallest file, convert to WebP at 85 percent quality. For a photo you will print, use JPG at 92 percent or PNG.
content.limit: GIF output is a still image, not an animation. ICO files are square, so wide images are fitted inside the square. JPEG-compressed TIFF files cannot be decoded here. AVIF output needs a browser that can save AVIF, and some browsers cannot.
content.example: A 2 MB PNG screenshot converted to WebP at 85 percent quality becomes a much smaller file that still looks the same on screen.
faq: Can I convert several images at once

Yes. Tick Batch mode, choose all the images, then press Convert Image. Each image is converted in turn and the results are downloaded together as one ZIP file, with the same name as each original image and the new extension.
Does it keep my photo details

When you convert a JPG to a JPG and tick Keep EXIF, the photo details from the original file are copied into the new file. If the photo was rotated, the orientation tag is reset so the picture does not turn sideways again in other apps.
Why is my TIFF not converting

Most TIFF files work, including uncompressed, LZW and deflate types. A TIFF that holds a JPEG-compressed image cannot be decoded here, so convert it to an uncompressed TIFF in another app first and then try again.
Which format should I choose

Use JPG for photos and WebP when you want the smallest file for the web. Use PNG when you need transparency or sharp text. Use BMP or GIF only when another app asks for that exact format, and ICO for app icons.

short.en: Read text from an image.

steps: Choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image with the file button. Clear printed text on a straight page reads best.
Pick the language of the text, or choose Auto-detect to let the tool work it out from the script it sees.
Press Read Text from Image and wait. The first run downloads language data, so it takes longer.
Read the words below the button. Words the tool is unsure about are highlighted, so you can check them.
Press Copy text for plain text, or Copy with line breaks to keep the layout of the original page.

content.use: Image to Text reads the printed words in a picture and gives you text you can copy. Before reading, it tidies the image for you: it fixes sideways photos from their EXIF orientation, straightens pages that were scanned at a slight angle, turns the picture grey, sharpens the contrast and enlarges small images so the letters are clearer. It can work out the language by itself when you choose Auto-detect, and it shows every word with a confidence mark, highlighting the words it is unsure about so you can check those against the picture. The recognised text stays on your device, and nothing is uploaded anywhere.
content.tip: Crop the image to just the text before reading it, and use a photo taken straight above the page. Handwriting reads poorly, so printed text works best.
content.limit: It reads printed text, not handwriting. Blurry photos, very small text and fancy fonts read badly. Urdu and Arabic read best when the page is straight and the letters are large.
content.example: A photo of a printed receipt reads as lines of text you can paste into a spreadsheet, with the shop name, items and total kept in order.
faq: How does auto-detect language work

The tool looks at the shapes of the letters and works out which script they belong to, then picks the matching language. English, Urdu and Arabic are covered, and it falls back to English when it cannot tell.
What do highlighted words mean

A highlighted word is one the tool is unsure about, usually because the letters were faint, blurred or partly covered. Compare those words with the picture and fix them by hand before you use the text.
Can it read handwriting
No, it is built for printed text only, and handwriting usually comes out wrong. For a handwritten note, type the words yourself or use the camera app on your phone, which is made for that job.
Why is the first run slow
The first time you use it, the tool downloads the language data it needs, which can take a minute on a slow connection. Later runs reuse the downloaded data, so they start much faster.

tools.meta_description: Read text from an image with OCR, free in your browser. Best on clear printed text; needs a language download first.

short.en: Text or URL as QR code.

steps: Pick what the QR code is for: a link, Wi-Fi, a contact, an email, a message, a phone number, a place or a payment.
Fill in the fields for that type.
Pick a size, an error-correction level and colours, and add a logo if you like.
Press Generate QR Code.
Download the code as PNG or SVG, and run Scan test to check it reads back.
tools.meta_description: Generate QR codes from text or a URL, free in your browser. Download your QR code as a PNG instantly.

content.use: QR Code Generator makes a QR code that a phone camera can read, for a link, a Wi-Fi network, a contact, an email, a text message, a phone number, a place or a payment. A shop owner prints a code that joins customers to the shop Wi-Fi. A freelancer puts a code on a business card that saves their contact details. You can pick the size, the error-correction level, the colours and a logo in the middle, and download it as a PNG or a crisp SVG for printing. The Scan test reads the code back to check it works. Everything runs in your browser, so nothing is uploaded and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use error-correction level H when you add a logo or print the code small, because the code can still be read when part of it is covered or damaged. Test the code with Scan test and with your own phone camera before you print it. Keep the light colour pale and the dark colour dark, or phones will struggle to read it.
content.limit: The code holds the text you type, and very long text makes a denser code that is harder to scan, so keep it short. A logo in the middle can make the code unreadable, even at a high error-correction level, so always test it. Payment QR formats differ by app, so paste the payment link or detail exactly as the app gives it. The scan test reads the code in your browser, which is a check, not a guarantee that every phone will read it.
content.example: A code for https://ak-premium.vercel.app at 320 px with error correction M scans in a second on most phones, and downloads as a PNG or an SVG.
faq: What error-correction level should I pick?
M is balanced and suits most codes. L holds the most data but breaks easily. Q and H survive damage and logos better, so pick H when you add a logo or print the code small.
Will my QR code work after I print it?
Yes, if it is printed big enough and sharp. Download the SVG for printing, because it stays crisp at any size. Test the printed code with your phone camera before you hand it out.
Why does Scan test say it cannot read the code?
The code may be too dense, too small, or the colours may be too close together. Try a bigger size, a higher error-correction level, darker dark colours and paler light colours, then test it again.
Does the QR code expire or track scans?
No. The code is just the text you typed, drawn as squares. It never expires, it is not stored anywhere, and no one can track who scans it, because nothing is uploaded.

short.en: Strong random passwords, instantly.

tools.meta_description: Generate strong random passwords instantly, free in your browser. Passwords are created locally, never sent anywhere.
steps: Pick a mode: random password, passphrase, pronounceable or PIN.
For a random password, set the length and tick the character sets to use.
For a passphrase, pick how many words and a separator.
Press Generate Password.
Copy the password and save it in a password manager. Never share it.

content.use: Password Generator makes a strong password in your browser, so you never have to think one up yourself. A random password mixes letters, numbers and symbols at the length you choose. A passphrase joins plain words, such as correct horse battery staple, which is easy to remember and hard to guess. A pronounceable password is easy to say and type, and a PIN is digits only for a phone lock. Every password comes with a strength meter and a crack-time estimate that run on your device. Nothing is uploaded or stored, so your password never leaves your browser and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use a random password of 16 characters or more for important accounts, and a different password for every account. A passphrase of 6 words is a good choice for a master password you must remember. Save every password in a password manager, and never reuse a password across accounts, because one leak then opens them all.
content.limit: The generator makes passwords, but it cannot store them, so copy each password into a password manager straight away. The strength meter is an estimate from a well-known library, not a guarantee, and a password is only as safe as the account it protects. A PIN is only for places that ask for digits, and it is far weaker than a password of the same length.
content.example: A 16-character random password with all four character sets scores Very strong, and the meter says an attacker guessing 10,000 passwords a second would need centuries to crack it.
faq: How strong is a passphrase of 6 words?
About 62 bits of entropy, because each word adds about 10.3 bits. That is far stronger than a short password, and much easier to remember. Use 6 words for a master password you must type yourself.
Where do the passphrase words come from?

From a 1,296-word sample of the EFF large wordlist, which the EFF publishes under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. The words are picked at random in your browser, so no two passphrases are alike.
Is my password sent anywhere?
No. The password is made in your browser with your device random numbers, and it is never uploaded or stored. The strength meter also runs on your device. Close the page and the password is gone.
What does the crack-time estimate mean?
It is how long an attacker guessing 10,000 passwords a second would need to find your password. Centuries means the password is strong. Seconds or minutes means you should make a longer one.

short.en: Words, characters, reading time.

tools.meta_description: Count words, characters and reading time, free in your browser. Paste text and see the counts instantly.
steps: Type or paste your text in the box.
Read the live counts below the box: Words, Characters, Characters (no spaces), Sentences, Paragraphs and Reading time.
Edit the text in the box and the counts update with every keystroke.

content.use: Word Counter counts the words, characters, sentences and paragraphs in your text as you type, so you can check a limit before you submit. A student checks that an essay is under 500 words. A job applicant checks that a cover letter fits the limit. A writer checks the reading time of an article before publishing it. The counts update live with every keystroke, so there is nothing to press. Reading time is worked out at 200 words per minute, which is a normal reading speed. The text never leaves your browser.
content.tip: Paste the final text, not a draft with notes, because everything in the box is counted. If the word count looks high, check for extra spaces or repeated paragraphs at the end.
content.limit: The tool counts what you type; it does not check spelling, grammar or meaning. Reading time is a rough guide at 200 words per minute and is rounded up to whole minutes. Paragraphs are counted by blank lines between blocks of text.
content.example: Pasting a 400-word essay shows Words: 400, Reading time: 2 min, because 400 words at 200 words per minute takes 2 minutes.
faq: How is reading time worked out?
At 200 words per minute, rounded up to whole minutes. A 400-word text shows 2 minutes, and a 250-word text shows 2 minutes as well.
What counts as a paragraph?
A block of text separated by a blank line. Pressing Enter once inside a paragraph does not start a new one; you need an empty line between blocks.
Do spaces count as characters?
Both counts are shown. Characters counts everything including spaces, and Characters (no spaces) counts letters and punctuation only.
Is there a limit on how much text I can paste?
No fixed limit. Very long text still counts, because the counting happens in your browser as you type.

short.en: Format, repair, validate and query JSON.

tools.meta_description: Format, minify, repair, sort and validate JSON, free in your browser. JSON Schema validation, JSONPath queries and a tree view included.
steps: Paste your JSON text in the box.
Press Format to tidy it, Minify to shrink it, Repair to fix common mistakes, Sort Keys to order the keys, or Tree View to explore it.
Paste a JSON Schema and press Validate with Schema to check the data against it, or type a JSONPath query and press Run Query to pull out matching values. Press Copy Result to copy the output.

content.use: JSON Formatter tidies, shrinks, repairs or checks JSON text, which is the data format used by most websites and apps. A student formats a messy API response so it is easy to read. A developer minifies a settings file before putting it in a project. An office worker validates a data file before sending it to a colleague. Format adds line breaks and a 2-space indent so the structure is clear. Minify removes all extra spaces so the file is as small as possible. Validate tells you whether the JSON is correct and shows the exact error if it is not. Repair fixes common mistakes such as missing quotes or trailing commas. Validate with Schema checks the data against a JSON Schema. Run Query pulls out values with a JSONPath expression, and Tree View shows the structure as a folding list.
content.tip: Press Validate first when you get an error from another app. The error message names the problem, such as a missing comma or an extra bracket, so you can fix that exact spot. If the JSON is almost right but will not parse, try Repair — it fixes missing quotes, trailing commas and single quotes.
content.limit: Repair fixes common mistakes, but it cannot guess what a badly broken file was meant to say — always read the repaired result before you use it. Schema validation follows JSON Schema 2020-12. JSONPath follows the jsonpath-plus syntax. The tool does not run code or call any server; everything happens in your browser, and very large files may be slow.
content.example: Pasting {"name":"Ali","age":25} and pressing Format shows the same data on separate lines with a 2-space indent, easy to read. Pasting {'name': 'Ali',} and pressing Repair gives back valid JSON with double quotes and no trailing comma.
faq: What does Repair fix?

Common mistakes: single quotes instead of double quotes, missing quotes around keys, trailing commas, and missing commas between values. It does not fix a file that is missing whole parts, and you should always read the repaired result before using it.
What does Validate with Schema do?

It checks your JSON against a JSON Schema you paste in, following JSON Schema 2020-12. If the data does not match, it lists each problem, such as a missing required field or a wrong type, with the path to the value.
How do I use Run Query?
Type a JSONPath expression, for example $.store.book[*].title, and press Run Query. It returns every matching value as a list. The syntax follows jsonpath-plus.
What does the duplicate keys warning mean?

The same key appears twice in one object, for example two "name" fields. When JSON is read, only the last value is kept, so the first one is lost. The warning shows the key and the line number so you can fix it.

short.en: Encode or decode Base64 text.

tools.meta_description: Encode or decode Base64 text, free in your browser. Convert text both ways instantly, with no sign-up.
steps: Type or paste your text in the box.
Press Encode to turn it into Base64, or Decode to turn Base64 back into text.
Press Copy Result to copy the output.

content.use: Base64 turns text into a safe code made of letters, numbers and a few symbols, and turns that code back into text. A developer encodes a token to paste into a settings file. A student decodes a Base64 string from a class example to see the original message. An office worker encodes a short note to send through a system that only accepts plain letters. The tool handles any language, including Urdu, because it encodes the text as UTF-8 first. Encode and Decode both run in your browser, so your text is never uploaded.
content.tip: Base64 is a code, not encryption. Anyone can decode it, so do not use it to hide a password or a secret. Use it only to move text safely through systems that cannot handle special characters.
content.limit: Base64 is not encryption and not a password. Anyone who sees the code can decode it. Decoding only works on valid Base64 text; anything else shows an error with the reason.
content.example: Typing 'hello' and pressing Encode gives 'aGVsbG8='. Pressing Decode on 'aGVsbG8=' gives back 'hello'.
faq: Is Base64 a way to hide a password?
No. Base64 is a code anyone can reverse. It only changes how the text looks, so never use it to protect a secret. Use a real password manager for passwords.
Can I encode Urdu text?
Yes. The tool encodes text as UTF-8 first, so Urdu and other languages encode and decode correctly.
Why does Decode show an error?
The text is not valid Base64. Check for missing characters, extra spaces or a cut-off string, then try again.
What is Base64 used for?
Moving text safely through systems that only accept plain letters and numbers, such as settings files, tokens and email attachments.

short.en: Change text case, four ways.

tools.meta_description: Change text case four ways — upper, lower, title and sentence case — free in your browser.
steps: Type or paste your text in the box.
Press UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case or Sentence case.
Press Copy Result to copy the changed text.

content.use: Case Converter changes the capital letters in your text, so you can fix a heading, a title or a whole paragraph in one click. A student turns a shouty heading into normal title case for an assignment. An office worker turns a lowercase notice into uppercase for a poster. A shop owner turns a product name into sentence case for a price list. The four buttons cover the common cases: all capitals, all lower case, capitals on every word, and a capital only at the start of each sentence. The changed text appears below, ready to copy.
content.tip: Use Title Case for headings and names, and Sentence case for normal paragraphs. If the result looks wrong, check the original text for extra spaces, because they can split words the tool treats separately.
content.limit: The tool changes letter case only. It does not fix spelling, punctuation or spacing. Title Case capitalises every word, including small words like 'and' and 'of', so you may need to fix those by hand.
content.example: Pasting 'hello world' and pressing Title Case gives 'Hello World'. Pressing UPPERCASE on the same text gives 'HELLO WORLD'.
faq: What does Title Case do?
It puts a capital letter at the start of every word, so 'hello world' becomes 'Hello World'. Small words like 'and' are also capitalised, so fix those by hand if needed.
What does Sentence case do?
It puts a capital at the start of each sentence and lower case elsewhere, so 'HELLO. HOW ARE YOU?' becomes 'Hello. How are you?'
Can I convert only part of my text?
No. The whole text in the box is converted at once. Paste only the part you want to change, then copy the result back.
Does the tool change my original text?
No. Your pasted text stays in the top box. The changed text appears below it, so you can copy it without losing the original.

short.en: Secure random UUIDs, instantly.

tools.meta_description: Generate secure random UUIDs instantly, free in your browser. Unique IDs created locally on your device.
steps: Press Generate UUID for one ID, or Generate 5 for five at once.
Read the IDs shown in the box below.
Press Copy Result to copy the ID or IDs.

content.use: UUID Generator makes secure random IDs, called UUIDs, that you can use as unique keys in a database, a file name or a test. A developer makes an ID for each new record in an app. A student makes unique file names for assignment uploads. An office worker makes reference numbers for a set of documents. Each UUID is a 36-character code in the standard 8-4-4-4-12 pattern, made with secure random numbers from your browser. Press Generate UUID for one, or Generate 5 to get five at once. The IDs never leave your browser.
content.tip: Use Generate 5 when you need a batch of IDs, then copy them all at once. If two systems must never share an ID, generate fresh ones for each system instead of reusing the same ID.
content.limit: The tool makes version 4 random UUIDs only. It does not make IDs based on a name, a date or a counter, and it does not check whether an ID already exists in your database. The IDs are random, so two of them will not match by chance.
content.example: Pressing Generate UUID gives one 36-character ID in the standard 8-4-4-4-12 pattern, and pressing Generate 5 gives five IDs at once, one per line.
faq: What is a UUID?
A universally unique identifier: a 36-character random code in the pattern 8-4-4-4-12. It is used as a unique key when two records must never share an ID.
Are the UUIDs really unique?
They are random version 4 UUIDs, so the chance of two matching is so small it can be ignored. The tool does not check your database, so keep your own list if you must be certain.
Can I generate more than 5 at once?
No. The tool makes one UUID or five at a time. Press Generate 5 again for another batch.
Is my UUID private?
Yes. The IDs are made in your browser with secure random numbers. Nothing is sent to a server or stored anywhere.

short.en: CSV rows as JSON objects.

tools.meta_description: Convert CSV rows into JSON objects, free in your browser. Paste CSV and get clean JSON instantly.
steps: Choose a .csv file with the file button, or paste CSV text in the box. The first row must be the header.
Press Convert CSV to JSON.
Press Copy JSON to copy the result, or Download .json to save it as a file.

content.use: CSV to JSON turns rows of comma-separated data into a JSON list of objects, which is the format most apps and websites read. A developer turns a spreadsheet export into JSON for an app. A student turns survey results into JSON for a class project. An office worker turns a contact list into JSON to send to a developer. The first row of the CSV becomes the field names, and each row after it becomes one object with those names. The result is shown as tidy JSON with a 2-space indent, ready to copy or download.
content.tip: Make sure the first row holds your column names, because they become the JSON field names. If a row has a different number of values than the header, the tool stops and tells you which row is wrong.
content.limit: The CSV needs a header row and at least one data row. Every data row must have the same number of fields as the header, or the tool shows an error naming the row. All values stay as text; numbers are not converted to JSON numbers.
content.example: Pasting 'name,age' then 'Ali,25' and pressing Convert CSV to JSON gives a JSON list with one object, name Ali and age 25, shown with a 2-space indent.
faq: What does the first row become?
The field names of each object. 'name,age' as the first row makes objects with 'name' and 'age' fields.
Why did the tool say a row has the wrong number of fields?
That row has more or fewer values than the header row. Count the commas in that row and fix it, then convert again.
Are numbers kept as numbers?
No. All values stay as text in the JSON, so age 25 becomes "25" in quotes. Change the types in your app if you need real numbers.
Can I download the JSON as a file?
Yes. Press Download .json to save it, or press Copy JSON to copy the text into your own editor.

short.en: Compare two texts, line by line.

tools.meta_description: Compare two texts line by line and see what changed, free in your browser. Added and removed lines shown clearly.
steps: Paste the original text in the 'Original text' box.
Paste the changed text in the 'Changed text' box.
Press Compare Texts and read the Removed, Added and Unchanged lines shown below.

content.use: Text Diff Checker compares two versions of a text and lists the lines that were added, removed or kept, so you can see exactly what changed. A student compares a draft essay with the final version to check the edits. A teacher compares two versions of a worksheet to find new questions. An office worker compares an old price list with a new one to spot changed prices. The tool splits both texts into lines, matches them, and shows the lines that appear in only one version, plus a count of the lines that stayed the same.
content.tip: Paste the two versions in the right boxes: the older text first, the newer text second. If the result says 'No differences found', the two texts are identical line for line.
content.limit: The tool compares whole lines, not single words, and it matches lines by their text. A line that moved to another place but stayed the same is not listed as changed. The result is shown on the page and is not downloaded as a file.
content.example: Comparing a price list with 10 lines against a new list with 11 lines shows 1 line Added, 0 lines Removed, and 10 Unchanged lines.
faq: Does the tool show changed words inside a line?
No. It compares whole lines. If one word in a line changed, the whole old line is listed as Removed and the whole new line as Added.
What does 'Unchanged lines' mean?
The number of lines from the original text that also appear in the changed text. A line that moved to another place still counts as unchanged.
Can I compare two files instead of pasted text?
No. Paste the text into the two boxes. Copy the text from each file into the boxes first.
What happens if the two texts are identical?
The result says 'No differences found.' Nothing is listed as added or removed.

short.en: Exact age in years, months, days.

tools.meta_description: Calculate exact age in years, months and days, free in your browser. Enter a birth date and get the exact age.
steps: Pick your date of birth in the 'Date of birth' box.
Press Calculate Age, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read your exact age in years, months and days.

content.use: Age Calculator works out your exact age in years, months and days from your date of birth, so you do not have to count it yourself. A student checks their age for a form that asks for years and months. A parent checks a child's exact age for a school admission form. An office worker checks an employee's age for a retirement record. You pick the date of birth, and the tool counts the full years, the extra months and the remaining days up to today. The result updates live as soon as you change the date.
content.tip: Use the calendar picker in the date box instead of typing the date, so the format is always right. If the date is in the future, the tool shows an error instead of a negative age.
content.limit: The age is counted up to today, using your device's date. A future date of birth is not accepted. The tool gives years, months and days only; it does not give the age in weeks or total days.
content.example: Picking 1 January 2000 as the date of birth on 18 November 2026 gives an age of 26 years, 10 months and 17 days.
faq: How is the age worked out?
The tool counts full years from your date of birth to today, then the extra months and the remaining days. The result is exact to the day.
Can I enter a future date?
No. A date in the future is not accepted, because an age cannot be negative. Pick a date in the past.
Does the result update on its own?
Yes. The calculator recalculates live as soon as you change the date, so you do not need to press the button again.
Why does it show months and days too?
Because many forms ask for an exact age, such as 17 years and 6 months. Years alone would not be enough for those forms.

short.en: Percent, share, and change.

tools.meta_description: Calculate percentages, shares and percent change, free in your browser. Quick percent maths with no sign-up.
steps: Choose a calculation in the 'Calculation' list: X% of Y, X is what % of Y, or Percentage change from X to Y.
Type the two numbers in the X and Y boxes.
Press Calculate, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.

content.use: Percentage Calculator answers the three percentage questions people ask most often: what is a percent of a number, what percent one number is of another, and how much a number changed in percent. A shop owner works out a 10 percent discount on a price. A student works out what percent 45 marks is of 60. An office worker works out the percent rise in sales from last month to this month. You pick the calculation, type X and Y, and the tool shows the answer in a full sentence, such as '20% of 500 = 100'. The result updates live as you type.
content.tip: For a discount, use 'X% of Y' to find the amount to take off, then subtract it from the price yourself. For a rise or fall, use 'Percentage change from X to Y', where X is the old number and Y is the new one.
content.limit: The tool needs two numbers for every calculation. For 'X is what % of Y', Y cannot be zero. For percentage change, X cannot be zero. The answer is shown as plain text; it is not saved or rounded to a fixed number of decimals.
content.example: Choosing 'X% of Y' with X as 20 and Y as 500 shows '20% of 500 = 100'.
faq: How do I work out a 10 percent discount?
Choose 'X% of Y', set X to 10 and Y to the price. The answer is the discount amount. Subtract it from the price to get the price after discount.
What does 'X is what % of Y' mean?
It tells you what share X is of Y. With X as 45 and Y as 60, the answer is 75%, because 45 is three quarters of 60.
How do I work out a price rise in percent?
Choose 'Percentage change from X to Y'. Put the old price in X and the new price in Y. A rise shows as a positive percent and a fall as a negative one.
Why does it say Y cannot be zero?
Dividing by zero is not possible. For 'X is what % of Y', Y is the whole you compare against, so it must not be zero.

short.en: BMI and category from height, weight.

tools.meta_description: Calculate BMI and its category from height and weight, free in your browser. Instant, private, no sign-up.
steps: Type your height in centimetres in the 'Height (cm)' box.
Type your weight in kilograms in the 'Weight (kg)' box.
Press Calculate BMI, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.

content.use: BMI Calculator works out your Body Mass Index from your height and weight, and tells you which category it falls in. A student checks their BMI for a health assignment. A parent checks a teenager's BMI before a doctor's visit. An office worker checks their own BMI as part of a fitness plan. You type your height in centimetres and your weight in kilograms, and the tool divides the weight by the height in metres squared, then rounds the answer to one decimal. The categories are Underweight below 18.5, Normal below 25, Overweight below 30, and Obese at 30 and above.
content.tip: Measure your height and weight on the same day for a fair result. BMI is a rough guide, not a diagnosis; it does not account for muscle, age or body shape, so ask a doctor if you are worried about the result.
content.limit: BMI needs a positive height and weight; anything else shows an error. The result is a general guide only. It does not measure body fat, muscle or health, and it is not medical advice. The calculator uses centimetres and kilograms only.
content.example: A height of 170 cm and a weight of 65 kg gives a BMI of 22.5, which falls in the Normal category.
faq: How is BMI worked out?
Weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. The tool takes centimetres and converts them to metres for you, then rounds the answer to one decimal.
What do the categories mean?
Underweight is below 18.5, Normal is 18.5 to under 25, Overweight is 25 to under 30, and Obese is 30 and above. These are general ranges, not a diagnosis.
Is BMI the same as body fat?
No. BMI only uses height and weight. It does not measure fat, muscle or fitness, so a muscular person can have a high BMI and still be healthy.
Can I use feet and pounds?
No. This calculator takes height in centimetres and weight in kilograms only. Convert your measurements first if you use feet and pounds.

short.en: Monthly EMI, full schedule, extra payments.

tools.meta_description: Calculate monthly EMI, total interest and total payment, free in your browser. Plan a loan in seconds.
steps: Type the loan amount in the 'Loan amount' box.
Type the annual interest rate in percent and the loan period in years.
Add an extra monthly payment or a one-time lump sum if you plan to pay more than the EMI.

Press Calculate EMI, or just wait, because the result updates as you type. The result shows the monthly EMI, total payment, total interest and number of months, plus a year-by-year chart, a yearly summary and the full month-by-month schedule. Tick Compare with a second loan to compare two loans side by side, or press Download Schedule (CSV) to save the schedule.

content.use: Loan / EMI Calculator works out the monthly payment on a loan, using the standard EMI formula, so you can plan before you borrow. A family checks the monthly payment on a home loan before talking to a bank. A shop owner checks the EMI on a business loan for new stock. A student checks the EMI on a small loan for a laptop. You type the loan amount, the annual interest rate and the number of years. The tool shows the monthly EMI, the total amount you will pay, the total interest and the number of months, with a breakdown table below. Add an extra monthly payment or a lump sum to see how much interest you save and how many months you cut off the loan. The month-by-month schedule shows how much of each payment is interest and how much is principal, and the yearly chart shows the two side by side.
content.tip: Try a longer loan period to see the EMI fall, and notice that the total interest rises. Compare the total interest, not just the monthly EMI, when you choose between two loans. Even a small extra payment each month can cut months off a long loan — try it and watch the interest saved.
content.limit: The result is a guide based on a fixed interest rate and equal monthly payments. It does not include bank fees, taxes or changing rates, and it is not financial advice. The rate must be 0 or more, and the loan amount and years must be positive.
content.example: A loan of Rs 1,000,000 at 12 percent for 5 years gives a monthly EMI of Rs 22,244.45, a total payment of Rs 1,334,667 and total interest of Rs 334,667. Paying Rs 5,000 extra a month on that loan saves Rs 82,391.65 in interest and finishes the loan 14 months early.
faq: What is an EMI?
An Equated Monthly Instalment: the same amount you pay every month until the loan is finished. Each payment covers part of the interest and part of the loan amount.
What happens if the interest rate is 0?
The tool divides the loan amount by the number of months. A Rs 600,000 loan over 5 years at 0 percent gives an EMI of Rs 10,000 a month.
How does the extra payment work?

An extra monthly payment goes straight to the loan amount, on top of the EMI, and a lump sum is paid in the first month. The schedule is rebuilt with the extra money, and the result shows the interest saved, the months cut and the month you become debt-free.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is a calculation based on a fixed rate and equal payments. Banks add fees and may change rates, so ask the bank for the final figures before you borrow.

short.en: Weighted CGPA from course grades.

tools.meta_description: Calculate weighted CGPA from course grades and credits, free in your browser. Enter courses, get your CGPA.
steps: Type one course per line in the box, as: Course, credit hours, grade point. For example: Math, 3, 3.7
Press Calculate CGPA, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read your CGPA to 2 decimals and your total credit hours.

content.use: CGPA Calculator works out your weighted CGPA from your courses, so you can check your result without a spreadsheet. A student checks their CGPA at the end of a semester. A job applicant checks their CGPA before writing it on a resume. A parent checks a child's CGPA for a scholarship form. You type one course per line, with the course name, the credit hours and the grade point, separated by commas. The tool multiplies each grade point by its credit hours, adds them up and divides by the total credit hours, then shows the CGPA to 2 decimals.
content.tip: Type the grade point exactly as your university gives it, such as 3.7 for an A-. If a line is wrong, the tool names it in the error, so fix that line and press Calculate CGPA again.
content.limit: The tool uses the grade points you type; it does not convert letter grades for you. Each line must have exactly three parts: course name, credit hours and grade point. Credit hours must be above zero and grade points cannot be negative.
content.example: Typing 'Math, 3, 3.7' and 'English, 3, 3.3' gives a CGPA of 3.50 across 6 credit hours.
faq: How do I write a course line?
One course per line as: Course, credit hours, grade point. For example: Math, 3, 3.7. The course name can be anything; the numbers must be in the right order.
Does the tool convert A, B and C grades?
No. It uses the grade points you type. Convert your letter grades to grade points first, using your university's scale, then enter the numbers.
What if one of my lines is wrong?
The tool shows an error naming the exact line, such as 'Invalid course line: Math, 3'. Fix that line and press Calculate CGPA again.
Why is the CGPA weighted?
Because a 3-credit course counts more than a 1-credit course. Each grade point is multiplied by its credit hours before the average is worked out.

short.en: Bill items, tax and total PDF.

content.use: An invoice generator is for freelancers, shops and small businesses that need a clean bill for a client: the work done, the quantity, the price, the tax and the total, as a PDF that can be sent on WhatsApp or email.
content.tip: Enter one item per line as item, quantity, price. Choose a template before you download. Template 2 has a coloured header and a notes line, Template 1 is plain and simple.
content.limit: The invoice is a simple formatted PDF, not a Word template or an accounting file. It does not store your invoices, and it does not calculate GST rules for you.
content.example: Design work, 2, 5000 with 0% tax gives a subtotal of 10,000 and a total of 10,000.
faq: Can I add tax to my invoice?
Yes. Enter the tax percentage and the tool adds it to the subtotal before showing the total.
Are there different invoice templates?
Yes, two. Template 1 is a plain, simple invoice. Template 2 has a coloured header and a notes line for payment details.
Can I see the total before downloading?
Yes. Press Calculate Summary first. The summary box shows each item, the subtotal, the tax and the total, so you can check the numbers.
Does it work out GST for me?
No. You enter the tax percentage yourself, and the tool adds it to the subtotal. It does not know the GST rules for your business.

tools.meta_description: Generate a bill with items, tax and total as a PDF, free in your browser. A clean invoice for your business.
steps: Type the Business name, Client name and Invoice date.
Choose Template 1 (plain and simple) or Template 2 (coloured header, with a Notes field) in the Template list.
List the items, one per line, as: Item name, quantity, price.
Type the Tax percent, press Calculate Summary to check the totals, then press Download Invoice PDF.

short.en: Clean PDF resume, quickly.

content.use: A resume builder is for a job seeker who needs a clean, one-page resume quickly: name, job title, contact details, skills and experience, as a PDF that can be attached to an application.
content.tip: Keep the experience short and specific, with numbers where you can: how many records, how many reports, how much time saved. Choose a template before you download.
content.limit: The resume is a simple formatted PDF, not a Word template. It does not store your resume, and it does not write the content for you.
