content.example: A data analyst resume with a name, title, email, phone, skills and two jobs becomes a clean PDF in one click.
faq: Are there different resume templates?
Yes, two. Template 1 is a classic single-column resume. Template 2 has a coloured header and a different skills layout.
Can I edit the resume after downloading it?
The PDF is not editable. If you need changes, edit the fields on this page and download it again.
What do I put in the skills box?
Your skills separated by commas, such as Excel, Power BI, Reporting. The template lays them out for you in the downloaded PDF.
Can I add a photo to my resume?
No. There is no photo field. The resume has your name, job title, contact details, skills and experience only, with nothing else on the page.

tools.meta_description: Build a clean PDF resume quickly, free in your browser. Add your name, skills and experience, then download.
steps: Type your Full name, Job title, Email, Phone and Skills (comma-separated).
Choose Template 1 (classic single column) or Template 2 (coloured header, skills as bullets) in the Template list.
Write your experience in the Experience box.
Press Download Resume PDF and save the file.

short.en: Palette from one base color.

tools.meta_description: Create a colour palette from one base colour, free in your browser. Complementary, analogous and triadic palettes.
steps: Pick a base colour, or type one as hex, rgb(), hsl() or a colour name.
Choose a harmony, or leave All harmonies to see every set at once.
Press Generate Palette and click any swatch to copy its hex code.
Or choose a photo and read its main colours with the eyedropper.
Download the palette as CSS variables, a Tailwind config or a PNG image.

content.use: Color Palette builds a set of colours that go well together from one base colour. A designer picks a brand colour and gets matching colours for buttons, headings and backgrounds. A shop owner picks the shop main colour and gets shades for the website. Each palette comes with a 50 to 900 shade scale, and a contrast check that says whether the colour reads well on white and on black. You can also read the main colours out of a photo, or export the palette as CSS variables, a Tailwind config or a PNG image. Everything runs in your browser, so nothing is uploaded and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Start from the colour you already use, such as your logo or brand colour, and try the monochromatic harmony for a calm look or complementary for a bold one. Use the contrast check before you put text on a colour: AA is the minimum for normal text, and AAA is better. Copy a swatch by clicking it, and export the CSS variables to paste straight into your stylesheet.
content.limit: The palette is built from colour maths, not from a designer, so the sets are a starting point and you should check them by eye. The eyedropper reads the main colours of a photo, but a busy photo may give colours that do not go together. Contrast is checked against plain white and black only, not against other colours in the palette.
content.example: Starting from indigo #4f46e5 gives a complementary palette with a warm orange, a full 50 to 900 shade scale, and a contrast reading that says it passes AA on white.
faq: What do AA and AAA mean for contrast?
They are WCAG grades for how easy text is to read. AA needs a contrast of 4.5 to 1 for normal text and 3 to 1 for large text. AAA needs 7 to 1 for normal text and 4.5 to 1 for large text.
Can I type a colour name instead of hex?
Yes. Type a name such as teal, navy or crimson, or a hex code such as #4f46e5, or rgb() or hsl() values. The tool reads all four, and the colour picker stays as a quick way to choose by eye.
How does the photo eyedropper work?
Choose a photo and the tool reads its six main colours with a small library called color-thief. The colours appear as a palette you can click to copy. Your photo never leaves your browser.
What do I get when I export the palette?
CSS variables give you a :root block with every colour, the Tailwind config gives you a brand scale from 50 to 900, and the PNG image gives you a swatch sheet you can share or print.

short.en: Convert Marla, Kanal, Acre, sq ft, sq yd and sq m.

steps: Enter the area in the unit you have.
Pick the unit you are converting from (Marla, Kanal, Acre, square feet, square yards or square metres).
Press Convert Land Area. All six units are shown at once.

content.use: A land converter is for the units used in Pakistan property deals: Marla, Kanal, Acre, square feet, square yards and square metres. A buyer, a seller, a patwari or a property dealer uses it to check that a 10 Marla plot and a 1 Kanal plot are being compared fairly.
content.tip: Enter the area in the unit you have, and the tool shows all the other units at once. 1 Kanal is 20 Marla, and 1 Acre is 8 Kanal.
content.limit: The tool converts area only. It does not give a price, a location, or legal advice about a plot, and it uses the standard Punjab unit sizes.
content.example: 1 Kanal is 20 Marla, 5,445 square feet and 605 square yards.
faq: How many Marla are in 1 Kanal?
20 Marla. 1 Marla is 272.25 square feet, so 20 Marla is 5,445 square feet.
How many Kanal are in 1 Acre?
8 Kanal. 1 Acre is 43,560 square feet.
How many square yards are in 1 Kanal?
605 square yards. 1 Kanal is 5,445 square feet, and 1 square yard is 9 square feet, so 5,445 divided by 9 is 605.
Can I convert from square feet?
Yes. Choose Square feet in the From list and enter the area. The tool shows the same area in Marla, Kanal, Acre, square yards and square metres.

short.en: FBR salary tax, monthly and annual, with take-home pay.

steps: Enter your gross monthly salary in rupees.
Pick the tax year. Tax Year 2027 (FY 2026-27) is the current year.
Tick Compare Tax Year 2026 vs 2027 to see both years side by side, or Compare with a second salary to compare two salaries.
Press Calculate Tax. The page shows a payslip-style result — gross, tax, take-home and effective rate — plus the slab breakdown.

content.use: A Pakistan salary tax calculator is for checking how much income tax is taken from a monthly salary, and what the take-home pay is. It is used before accepting a job offer, at the start of a tax year, and when a salary changes. Comparing two tax years shows whether a new budget raised or lowered your tax; comparing two salaries shows what a raise is really worth after tax.
content.tip: Enter your gross monthly salary and pick the tax year. The current year is Tax Year 2027 (FY 2026-27). Tick the compare boxes before you press Calculate Tax, and the comparison table appears below the result.
content.limit: This is an estimate only, using FBR slabs for salaried individuals. It does not include rebates, allowances, other income, or tax already deducted. It is not tax advice. Tax Year 2025 is not included because its slabs were not directly verified from an official FBR document. For Tax Year 2026, a 9% surcharge applies where annual taxable income is above Rs 10,000,000; it was withdrawn for Tax Year 2027.
content.example: A monthly salary of Rs 200,000 is Rs 2,400,000 a year. In Tax Year 2027 the tax is Rs 156,000 a year, about Rs 13,000 a month. The same salary in Tax Year 2026 gives Rs 162,000 a year, so Tax Year 2027 is Rs 6,000 a year less for this salary.
faq: Which tax year should I choose?
Tax Year 2027 (FY 2026-27) is the current year as of November 2026. Tax Year 2026 (FY 2025-26) is there for last year's figures.
Is this the exact tax I will pay?
No. It is an estimate from the FBR slabs only. Your employer may apply rebates and allowances, so check your payslip or ask a tax adviser for the exact figure.
How does the year comparison work?
Tick Compare Tax Year 2026 vs 2027 before you press Calculate Tax. The table shows the tax, surcharge, monthly tax, take-home pay and effective rate for both years, side by side, for the same salary.
What is the surcharge line?

For Tax Year 2026, a 9% surcharge is charged on the tax where annual taxable income is above Rs 10,000,000. It is shown as its own line in the result and the breakdown when it applies. The surcharge was withdrawn for Tax Year 2027, so it never appears there.

short.en: Zakat at 2.5% with nisab by gold or silver rate.

steps: Enter your cash and bank balance, and subtract any debts.
Enter your gold and silver in tola, with the current rate per tola for each.
Press Calculate Zakat. The page shows net wealth, the nisab and the Zakat due at 2.5%.

content.use: A Zakat calculator is for working out the Zakat due on cash, gold and silver held for one lunar year. It is used in Ramadan and at the end of a lunar year, when a person checks whether their wealth has reached the nisab.
content.tip: Enter the current rate per tola for gold and silver, because the nisab depends on today's prices. The calculator uses the silver nisab (52.5 tola) when you give a silver rate.
content.limit: This is an estimate only, not religious advice. The nisab is 7.5 tola gold or 52.5 tola silver, and Zakat is 2.5% of net zakatable wealth. The government bank-deduction nisab for Ramadan 2026 was reported as Rs 503,529, but that figure was not directly verified from an official source, so it is shown only as reported.
content.example: Cash and gold worth Rs 1,000,000 above the nisab gives Rs 25,000 Zakat at 2.5%.
faq: What is the nisab?
The nisab is the minimum wealth above which Zakat is due: 7.5 tola of gold or 52.5 tola of silver. If your wealth is below it, no Zakat is due.
How much Zakat do I pay?
2.5% of your net zakatable wealth, after subtracting debts, once it has been held for one lunar year.
Can I set my own nisab?
Yes. Enter it in the Custom nisab box. If you leave it empty, the calculator uses the silver nisab from the silver rate you entered.
Does my house or car count?
No. The calculator only counts cash, gold and silver. Your house, car and other personal items are not entered and are not counted.

content.use: Amount to words is for invoices, cheques and receipts, where an amount must be written out in words as well as figures. A shop, a school and a freelancer all use it so the amount cannot be changed by adding a digit.

Does it work for paisa too?

Does it write the amount in Urdu too?

What is the largest amount it can write?

What reading speed does it use?
200 words per minute, which is a normal adult reading speed. Your own speed may be faster or slower.
Can I paste English text too?

content.use: A marks and merit calculator is for students applying to college or university in Pakistan, where admission depends on a weighted aggregate: Matric marks, FSc marks and an entry test, each with its own weight. It is also used for any percentage or weighted score.
content.tip: Enter the obtained and total marks for each part, and the weight for that part. The weights must add up to 100%. The tool shows each part's contribution and the final aggregate.
content.limit: The tool uses a generic weighted formula: sum of (obtained / total x 100 x weight / 100). It does not know any university's own formula, so check the official merit formula for the place you are applying to.
content.example: Matric 900/1100 at 10% weight, FSc 950/1100 at 40% weight, and an entry test 150/200 at 50% weight gives an aggregate of about 80.2%.
faq: What is a merit aggregate?
A merit aggregate combines several scores into one percentage, giving each part a weight. A part with 50% weight matters five times as much as a part with 10% weight.
What if my weights do not add up to 100%?
The tool stops and tells you the total, because an aggregate only makes sense when the weights add up to 100%. Fix the weights and try again.
How many parts can I enter?
Up to 3 parts. Fill in the obtained marks, total marks and weight for each part you use, and leave the rest blank.
Does it show each part's share?
Yes. The result lists every part with its percentage and its contribution. Part 1 at 81.82 percent with 10 percent weight gives 8.18.

short.en: Turn JPG images into one PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn JPG images into one PDF, one photo per page, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose one or more JPG files.

Leave Auto-rotate photos from EXIF data on so phone photos come out upright, or turn it off.
Tick Grayscale for black-and-white pages and set JPEG quality with the slider.
Press Convert JPG to PDF and save the file.

content.use: Turns JPG photos into a single PDF, one photo per page or two or four in a grid. It is made for the everyday jobs: sending a set of photos as one file, printing pictures on A4 or Letter paper, or turning phone photos into a document you can share. Phone photos are rotated upright automatically using the EXIF orientation stored by the camera, so sideways pictures come out the right way up. You can print each photo full-size at its natural size, choose JPEG quality to balance file size against sharpness, or switch on grayscale for a black-and-white document. Everything runs in your browser, and the photos never leave your device.
content.tip: For a photo-book look, use 1 image per page with Print size set to Fit to page; for a contact sheet, use 4 per page.
content.limit: Photos are re-encoded as JPEG, so a very low quality value loses detail. PNG, WebP and HEIC files are not accepted here, use PNG to PDF for PNG files.
content.example: Three holiday photos become a 3-page A4 PDF: choose the files, leave 1 per page and Auto-rotate on, press Convert JPG to PDF.
faq: Will my phone photos come out the right way up?
Yes, when Auto-rotate photos from EXIF data is on. The tool reads the orientation your camera stored in the photo and turns the picture upright before placing it on the page.
What does the Full size print option do?
It places each photo at its natural size instead of fitting it to the page, at 72 DPI and full JPEG quality. Use it when you want the photo printed exactly as taken, without scaling.
Can I put four photos on one page?
Yes. Set Images per page to 4 and the photos are placed in a two-by-two grid, each in its own cell. Choose 2 for two photos side by side.
Does JPG to PDF keep the original photo quality?

The photos are re-encoded as JPEG at the quality you choose, so at 92% and above the difference is hard to see. Full size keeps full quality; lower quality values make smaller files but softer detail.

short.en: Turn PNG images into one PDF.

tools.meta_description: Turn PNG images into one PDF, one image per page, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose one or more PNG files.
Pick Images per page (1, 2 or 4) and Page size (A4 or Letter).
Choose Transparency: keep it as-is, flatten onto white or black, or pick your own colour.
Tick Save images as JPEG inside the PDF for a smaller file, and set JPEG quality with the slider.
Press Convert PNG to PDF and save the file.

content.use: Turns PNG images into a single PDF, one image per page or two or four in a grid. Transparent areas are kept exactly as they are, so a logo with a see-through background stays see-through in the PDF, or they can be flattened onto white, black or a colour of your choice, handy when the PDF will be printed, because printers cannot print transparency. You can also save the images as JPEG inside the PDF for a smaller file, at a quality you choose, or tick Grayscale for a black-and-white document. Everything runs in your browser, and the images never leave your device.
content.tip: Keep transparency as-is for logos that will sit on a coloured page; flatten onto white when the PDF will be printed.
content.limit: Flattening onto a colour replaces transparent pixels permanently in the PDF. The save-as-JPEG option re-encodes images, so fine detail can soften at low quality.
content.example: A logo with a transparent background becomes a 1-page A4 PDF with the transparency kept, ready to place on a coloured letterhead.
faq: What happens to the transparent parts of a PNG?
By default nothing: transparent pixels stay transparent in the PDF, so whatever is behind the image shows through. Choose a flatten option only if you want a solid background instead.
Why flatten a PNG onto white?
Printers cannot print transparency, so a transparent area would come out white or patchy on paper. Flattening onto white first makes the printed result predictable.
When should I use the save as JPEG option?
When file size matters more than transparency. JPEG is much smaller than PNG for photos, but it cannot hold transparency, so the option also flattens the image first.
Can I mix PNG files of different sizes?
Yes. Each image is fitted into its own cell, so a mix of wide and tall images still lines up neatly in the grid you chose.

short.en: Render PDF pages as JPG images.

tools.meta_description: Render PDF pages as JPG images, with a download link per page and one ZIP file. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file.
Pick Resolution (72 to 300 DPI) and JPEG quality with the slider.
Set Pages to all, or a range such as 1-3, 5.
Optionally choose Resize to width and tick Grayscale.
Press Convert PDF to JPG, then download a single page or the ZIP of all pages.

content.use: Renders every page of a PDF as a JPG image, in your browser. It is made for sharing a page as a picture, posting a page on social media, or putting a page into a document that only accepts images. You choose the resolution from 72 DPI for a quick preview up to 300 DPI for print quality, and the JPEG quality to balance sharpness against file size. You can convert only the pages you need, shrink the images to a set width such as 800 or 1200 pixels, or switch on grayscale. One page downloads on its own; several pages come as a ZIP file.
content.tip: 150 DPI at 90% quality is a good balance for sharing; use 300 DPI when the image will be printed.
content.limit: JPG has no transparency and uses lossy compression, so fine text can soften at low quality. Very large PDFs at 300 DPI take a while and make big files.
content.example: Page 2 of a 5-page PDF becomes a 150 DPI JPG: choose the file, set Pages to 2, press Convert PDF to JPG.
faq: What DPI should I choose for PDF to JPG?
72 DPI is enough for a quick preview, 150 DPI looks good on screen and in most documents, and 300 DPI is for print. Higher DPI means sharper images and bigger files.
Can I convert only some pages to JPG?
Yes. Put the pages in the Pages box, for example 1-3, 5, and only those pages are rendered. Leave it as all to convert the whole PDF.
Why is there no ZIP when I convert one page?
When only one page is converted, the single JPG downloads directly, so no ZIP is needed. A ZIP is made only when two or more pages are converted.
Is JPG or PNG better for a PDF page?
JPG makes smaller files and is best for photos and sharing. PNG keeps sharper text and supports transparency, so use PDF to PNG when the page is mostly text or needs a transparent background.

short.en: Render PDF pages as PNG images.

tools.meta_description: Render PDF pages as PNG images, with a download link per page and one ZIP file. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file.
Pick Resolution (72 to 300 DPI).
Set Pages to all, or a range such as 1-3, 5.
Optionally choose Resize to width and tick Transparent background.
Set the File names pattern, then press Convert PDF to PNG and download a single page or the ZIP.

content.use: Renders every page of a PDF as a PNG image, in your browser. PNG keeps text sharp and supports transparency, so it is the better choice when the page is mostly text, a diagram or a logo. You choose the resolution from 72 DPI for a quick preview up to 300 DPI for print quality, convert only the pages you need, and shrink the images to a set width such as 800 or 1200 pixels. The file-name pattern names every image for you, report-p{nn}.png becomes report-p01.png, report-p02.png and so on, and one page downloads on its own while several pages come as a ZIP file.
content.tip: Use the file-name pattern report-p{nn}.png so the files sort in page order; {nn} becomes 01, 02 and so on.
content.limit: PNG files are larger than JPG. A transparent background only works where the page itself has no background colour, a page with a white background stays white.
content.example: A 3-page report becomes report-p01.png, report-p02.png and report-p03.png at 150 DPI.
faq: How does the file-name pattern work?

Type a pattern such as report-p{nn}.png and {nn} is replaced by the page number with a leading zero: 01, 02, 03. {n} gives 1, 2, 3 without the zero. Without a pattern the files are named by page number.
When is the background actually transparent?
Only when the PDF page itself has no background colour. A page drawn with a white background stays white, because there is nothing transparent to keep.
Can I convert only pages 2 and 4 to PNG?
Yes. Put 2, 4 in the Pages box and only those two pages are rendered. Ranges such as 1-3, 5 work too.
Why are PNG files bigger than JPG files?
PNG uses lossless compression, so it keeps every pixel exactly and stays sharp for text and diagrams. JPG throws away detail to save space, which is fine for photos but softens text.

tools.meta_description: Turn a saved HTML file into a PDF in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.

content.use: Turns pasted or uploaded HTML into a real rendered PDF, in your browser. Headings, bold text, lists and tables are drawn as they look on a page, and pictures embedded in the HTML appear in the PDF. Links in the HTML stay clickable in the PDF. It is made for saving a receipt, an invoice or a simple web page as a document you can share or print. Scripts are removed before rendering, so a saved page cannot run code on this site. If a page cannot be rendered, the tool falls back to plain text and says so honestly instead of failing.
content.tip: Save the page with its pictures embedded (data: URLs) before converting, or the pictures will be missing from the PDF.
content.limit: Only the HTML you paste or upload is converted, pasting a web address is not supported, and pages that need a server or a login cannot be converted. External pictures are not fetched. If the page cannot be rendered, the tool falls back to plain text and says so.
content.example: A saved invoice page with a table and a link becomes a 1-page A4 PDF with the table drawn as it looks and the link still clickable.
faq: Can I convert a web page by pasting its address?
No. This tool only converts HTML you paste or upload. A web address would need a server to fetch the page, and this site has no server, your files never leave your browser.
Why are the pictures missing from my PDF?
Pictures that live at a web address are not fetched, so they are skipped. Save the page with its pictures embedded in the file (data: URLs) and they will appear.
Are links in the HTML still clickable in the PDF?
Yes, when the page renders normally. Links to web pages and email addresses are added back to the PDF as clickable link areas on the right pages.
What happens if the page cannot be rendered?
The tool falls back to the plain text of the page and tells you it did so, instead of failing. A simpler saved page usually renders properly.

short.en: Save the images inside a PDF as PNG files.

tools.meta_description: Save the images embedded in a PDF as PNG files, one link per image and one ZIP file. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file.
Press Extract Images.
Download any image on its own from the list, or take the ZIP with all of them.
Check the list: it says which images came out in their original format and which were decoded to PNG.

content.use: Saves the pictures embedded inside a PDF, in your browser. JPEG, JPEG 2000 and JBIG2 pictures are saved in their original format and at their original resolution, byte for byte, so there is no quality loss from re-encoding. Other pictures are decoded and saved as PNG. Each image gets its own download link, with its page number, format and size shown next to it, and a ZIP with all the images downloads as well. It is made for recovering photos and logos from a PDF, or checking what pictures a document actually contains.
content.tip: JPEG pictures download in their original bytes, so there is no quality loss from re-encoding.
content.limit: Vector drawings (shapes and lines drawn by the PDF itself) are not pictures and are not extracted, use PDF to Images for a picture of the whole page. A JPEG with a transparency mask keeps its JPEG bytes but the mask is not kept. JBIG2 files are saved raw and need their globals segment to open in a viewer.
content.example: A 2-page brochure gives 3 images: 2 JPEGs in original format and 1 PNG, plus a ZIP with all three.
faq: What image formats can be extracted in their original form?
JPEG, JPEG 2000 and JBIG2 pictures are saved byte for byte in their original format. Flate and other pictures are decoded to PNG instead.
Why did I get a PNG instead of the original JPEG?
The picture was stored in the PDF with a filter that is not JPEG, so there are no original JPEG bytes to save. It is decoded to PNG, which keeps every pixel.
Can this extract vector drawings or logos?
No. Vector drawings are shapes and lines drawn by the PDF itself, not embedded pictures, so there is no image file to save. Use PDF to Images for a picture of the whole page.
Why does my PDF show no images at all?
The PDF may be text only, or made entirely of vector shapes. Try PDF to Images, which renders each page as a picture instead of looking for embedded files.

title.en: Add Header and Footer to PDF

short.en: Stamp header and footer text on every page.

tools.meta_description: Stamp the same header and footer text on every page of a PDF, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file.
Type Header text and Footer text, use {page} for the page number, {total} for the page count and {date} for today's date.
Pick the Font, Font size, Colour and Alignment.
Choose Pages: all pages, odd or even only, all except the first, or the first page only.
Tick Different header and footer on the first page and choose a logo if you need them, then press Add Header & Footer.

content.use: Stamps header and footer text on the pages of a PDF, in your browser. It is made for adding a running page count, a document title, a date or a confidentiality note to a report before sharing it. You choose the font, size, colour and alignment, and which pages get the stamp, all pages, odd or even pages only, all except the first page, or just the first page. The first page can have its own different header and footer, and a logo image can be placed at the header line. Placeholders do the counting for you: {page} becomes the page number, {total} the page count and {date} today's date.
content.tip: Type Page {page} of {total} in the footer for a running page count, and {date} in the header for the date the file was stamped.
content.limit: The header and footer are stamped on top of the page, so very long text is shrunk to fit and may cover page content near the edges. The logo is drawn at the header line only.
content.example: A 10-page report gets 'Confidential, Page 3 of 10' in the footer of every page and the company logo at the top left.
faq: What do {page}, {total} and {date} do?
{page} is replaced by the page number, {total} by the total number of pages, and {date} by today's date. So 'Page {page} of {total}' on page 3 of 10 becomes 'Page 3 of 10'.
Can the first page have a different header?
Yes. Tick 'Different header and footer on the first page' and type the first-page header and footer in the boxes that appear. Leave a box empty and nothing is stamped there on the first page.
Can I add a header to odd pages only?
Yes. Set Pages to 'Odd pages only' and the header and footer are stamped on pages 1, 3, 5 and so on. 'Even pages only' does the opposite.
Will the header cover text near the top of the page?
It can, because the header is stamped on top of the page. Keep headers short, or use 'All except the first page' so a title page stays clear.

short.en: Flatten form fields and annotations in a PDF.

tools.meta_description: Flatten a PDF so form fields become permanent text and annotations are removed. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file.
Pick what to flatten: form fields and annotations, form fields only, or annotations only.
Press Flatten PDF.
Read the field report below: it lists the original fields and how many annotations are left.
Download the field report (.txt) if you want a copy of what was flattened.

content.use: Makes form fields and annotations a permanent part of the page, so they can no longer be changed or removed. It is made for finalising a filled-in form before sending it, or locking comments and highlights into a document you are about to share. Form fields are flattened in the browser, and annotations are flattened with qpdf, which renders them into the page while keeping hyperlinks as links. You choose whether to flatten both, only the form fields, or only the annotations. A report lists the original fields and how many annotations remain, and you can download it as a text file.
content.tip: Choose 'Form fields only' when you want the filled-in answers kept but the annotations (comments and highlights) left editable.
content.limit: Flattening cannot be undone, keep the original file. Annotations with no appearance to draw are left in place, and the report says how many. Links are kept as links.
content.example: A filled application form is flattened so the answers can no longer be changed, and the field report lists the 8 fields that were flattened.
faq: What is the difference between flattening fields and annotations?

Flattening fields turns filled-in form boxes into ordinary page text, so the answers cannot be changed. Flattening annotations renders comments, highlights and stamps into the page itself. You can do either one or both.
Can I undo flattening?
No. Once the fields and annotations are part of the page, there is no way back, so keep the original file safe before you flatten.
Why are some annotations still there after flattening?
An annotation with no appearance to draw, nothing visible to render into the page, is left in place by qpdf. The report says how many are left.
Are hyperlinks kept when a PDF is flattened?
Yes. Link annotations are kept as links, so web addresses and email addresses in the document still work after flattening, exactly as they did before.

short.en: View and edit a PDF's title, author and more.

tools.meta_description: View and edit a PDF's title, author, subject and keywords, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file, the current metadata is shown above the form.
Pick the Preset: edit the fields below, or remove all personal metadata in one go.
Change the Title, Author, Subject, Keywords, Creator, Producer and dates.
Leave 'Also write these details into the XMP packet' ticked so readers can see them.
Press Update Metadata and save the file.

content.use: Shows and changes a PDF's title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer and dates, in your browser. It is made for fixing a wrong author name, adding keywords so a document is easier to find, or cleaning personal details out of a file before sharing it. The current details are shown when you choose the file, and the 'Remove all personal metadata' preset clears the title, author, subject, keywords, creator and the XMP packet in one go. The details are written into the file's info and, when the box is ticked, into its XMP packet too.
content.tip: Use 'Remove all personal metadata' before sharing a file outside your organisation, it clears title, author, subject, keywords, creator and the XMP packet in one go.
content.limit: The app that saves the file always writes its own name as Producer and the save time as the Modification Date in the file properties, those two values can only be kept in the XMP packet, not in the file properties.
content.example: A report's author is changed from a personal name to 'Reports Team' and the creation date is set to 1 January 2026.
faq: What is the XMP packet?

It is a block of metadata stored inside the PDF alongside the usual title and author details. Many readers and search tools read it, so this tool writes your details there as well as in the file properties.
Why does the Producer still show the old app name?

Every app that saves a PDF writes its own name as the Producer in the file properties, that cannot be avoided in a browser. Your Producer value is stored in the XMP packet instead, where a reader can still see it.
What does 'Remove all personal metadata' actually remove?
It clears the title, author, subject, keywords and creator, and deletes the XMP packet. The saved file still names the app that saved it as Producer and shows the save time as the dates.
Can I change the creation date of a PDF?
Yes. Set the Creation date field and it is saved in the file properties and the XMP packet. The Modification Date you type is kept in the XMP packet; the file properties always show the save time.

short.en: Scale every page to A4, Letter or Legal.

tools.meta_description: Scale every page of a PDF to A4, Letter or Legal, in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.
steps: Choose a PDF file.
Pick a Page size: A4, Letter, Legal, or Custom size with a width and height in millimetres.
Set Pages to all, or a range such as 1-3, 5, to resize only some pages.
Press Resize Pages and save the file.

content.use: Scales the pages of a PDF to A4, Letter, Legal or a custom size in millimetres, without turning them into pictures. The page content is scaled in place, so text stays selectable and drawings stay vector, nothing is re-rendered or blurred. Form fields and links are scaled with their pages, so a link or a field keeps working in the right place. You can resize the whole document or only the pages you choose, for example pages 2 to 3, while the rest keep their original size. Everything runs in your browser.
content.tip: Resize only the pages that need it, set Pages to 2-3 to leave the cover page at its original size.
content.limit: Pages are scaled to fit, so a landscape page on a portrait target gets side margins. Text inside a form field keeps its original font size, so shrinking a page a lot can clip field text. Pages whose content uses an encoding the tool cannot read are skipped and named in the status.
content.example: A 2-page PDF with Letter pages becomes A4: both pages are scaled to fit, the text stays selectable, and the link on page 2 still works.
faq: Does resizing turn my PDF pages into pictures?
No. The page content is scaled in place, so text stays selectable and drawings stay vector. Nothing is re-rendered, so the quality does not drop.
Do form fields and links still work after resizing?
Yes. Form fields and link areas are scaled by the same amount as their pages, so they stay in the right place and keep working.
Can I resize only some pages?
Yes. Put the pages in the Pages box, for example 2-3, and only those pages are resized. Leave it as all to resize the whole document.
Why was a page skipped during resizing?
A page is skipped when its content uses an encoding the tool cannot read, or when it has no content at all. The status names the skipped pages, and the rest are resized normally.

short.en: Turn PNG images into JPG.

tools.meta_description: Turn PNG images into JPG in your browser, free and private. Transparent parts become white.
steps: Choose a PNG image with the file button.
Set the quality with the slider. Lower quality gives a smaller file.
Pick a background colour for the see-through parts. JPG has no transparency.
Press Convert PNG to JPG.
Save the downloaded JPG, which has the same width and height as the PNG.

content.use: PNG to JPG turns a PNG picture into a JPG file, keeping the same width and height. A student turns a PNG screenshot into a JPG to upload to a portal that only takes JPG files. A shop owner turns product PNGs into JPGs so the shop loads faster. JPG files are smaller than PNG files, so they are easier to send and upload. The quality slider trades a little sharpness for a smaller file, and the background colour fills the see-through parts, because JPG has no transparency. Photos are turned the right way up from their photo data. The picture is converted in your browser, so your image is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use PNG to JPG when you need a smaller file for upload or sharing. If your PNG has transparency, remember the see-through parts become the background colour you pick, so convert to PNG instead if you need to keep transparency. For the sharpest result, start from a clear PNG; a blurry picture stays blurry after conversion.
content.limit: Only PNG images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. JPG has no transparency, so see-through parts of the PNG become the background colour you pick. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 PNG screenshot gives a 1200 by 800 JPG file that is much smaller and ready to upload.
faq: What happens to transparency in JPG?

It becomes the background colour you pick. JPG has no transparency, so the see-through parts of your PNG take that colour. White is the default. Convert to PNG or WebP instead if you need to keep the transparency.
Does the JPG keep the same size?
Yes. The width and height stay exactly the same as the PNG. Only the file format changes. Use Image Resizer if you also need a different size.
Can I convert several PNG images at once?
No. This page converts one PNG image at a time. Choose one image, press Convert PNG to JPG, save the result, then choose the next image.
What name does the JPG download with?
ak-premium-png-to-jpg.jpg. It has the same width and height as your PNG, and your original PNG file is not changed in any way.

short.en: Turn JPG images into PNG.

tools.meta_description: Turn JPG images into PNG in your browser, free and private. The picture keeps its size.
steps: Choose a JPG image with the file button.
Tick Save as PNG-8 if you want a much smaller file with 256 colours.
Press Convert JPG to PNG.
Save the downloaded PNG, which has the same width and height as the JPG.

content.use: JPG to PNG turns a JPG picture into a PNG file, keeping the same width and height. A designer turns a JPG logo into a PNG so it can sit on a coloured background without a white box. PNG keeps every pixel exactly, so it is the right choice when you need a clean image for editing or printing. The PNG-8 option uses only 256 colours, which makes the file much smaller, though a photo with smooth colour blends may show banding. Photos are turned the right way up from their photo data. The picture is converted in your browser, so your image is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use PNG-8 for logos, icons and simple graphics, where 256 colours are plenty and the file shrinks a lot. For a normal photo, leave PNG-8 unticked, because a photo needs far more than 256 colours to look smooth. If the PNG is bigger than the JPG you started from, that is normal: PNG does not throw away detail the way JPG does.
content.limit: Only JPG images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. A PNG file is usually bigger than the JPG it came from, because PNG keeps every pixel. PNG-8 keeps only 256 colours, so smooth photos may show banding. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 JPG photo gives a 1200 by 800 PNG file with the same picture, ready to edit or print.
faq: Why is the PNG bigger than my JPG?

PNG keeps every pixel exactly, while JPG throws away detail to save space. A photo converted to PNG is usually bigger than the JPG it came from. Tick PNG-8 if you want a smaller file and 256 colours are enough.
What is PNG-8 and when should I use it?
PNG-8 uses a palette of 256 colours instead of millions, so the file is much smaller. It suits logos, icons and simple graphics. A normal photo needs more colours, so leave PNG-8 unticked for photos.
Does the PNG keep the same size?
Yes. The width and height stay exactly the same as the JPG. Only the file format changes. Use Image Resizer if you also need a different size.
What name does the PNG download with?
ak-premium-jpg-to-png.png. It has the same width and height as your JPG, and your original JPG file is not changed in any way.

short.en: Turn WebP images into JPG.

tools.meta_description: Turn WebP images into JPG in your browser, free and private. Works for photos saved as WebP.
steps: Choose a WebP image with the file button.
Set the quality with the slider. Lower quality gives a smaller file.
Pick a background colour for the see-through parts. JPG has no transparency.
Press Convert WebP to JPG.
Save the downloaded JPG, which has the same width and height as the WebP.

content.use: WebP to JPG turns a WebP picture into a JPG file, keeping the same width and height. A shop owner turns WebP product photos into JPGs so they open in an older program that does not know WebP. JPG opens almost everywhere, so it is the safe choice when you are not sure what the other side can read. The quality slider trades a little sharpness for a smaller file, and the background colour fills the see-through parts, because JPG has no transparency. Photos are turned the right way up from their photo data. The picture is converted in your browser, so your image is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use WebP to JPG when the place you are sending the picture to does not accept WebP, such as an old portal, a printer or a program that only takes JPG. If the picture must stay small and the other side accepts WebP, keep it as WebP instead, because WebP is smaller than JPG at the same quality.
content.limit: Only WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. JPG has no transparency, so see-through parts of the WebP become the background colour you pick. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 WebP photo gives a 1200 by 800 JPG file that opens in almost any program.
faq: Why turn WebP into JPG at all?
Some portals, printers and older programs do not accept WebP yet. JPG opens almost everywhere, so converting is the safe choice when you are not sure what the other side can read.
What colour fills the see-through parts?
The background colour you pick fills the see-through parts, because JPG has no transparency. White is the default. Pick a colour that matches the page or document where the JPG will sit.
Will the picture stay the same size?
Yes. The width and height stay exactly the same as the WebP. Only the file format changes. Use Image Resizer if you also need a different size.
Can I convert several WebP images at once?
No. This page converts one WebP image at a time. Choose one image, press Convert WebP to JPG, save the result, then choose the next image.

short.en: Turn WebP images into PNG.

tools.meta_description: Turn WebP images into PNG in your browser, free and private. Transparency is kept.
steps: Choose a WebP image with the file button.
Tick Save as PNG-8 if you want a much smaller file with 256 colours.
Press Convert WebP to PNG.
Save the downloaded PNG, which has the same width and height as the WebP.

content.use: WebP to PNG turns a WebP picture into a PNG file, keeping the same width and height. A designer turns a WebP logo into a PNG so it can sit on a coloured background without a white box. PNG keeps every pixel exactly, so it is the right choice when you need a clean image for editing or printing, and it keeps WebP transparency. The PNG-8 option uses only 256 colours, which makes the file much smaller, though a photo with smooth colour blends may show banding. Photos are turned the right way up from their photo data. The picture is converted in your browser, so your image is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use PNG-8 for logos, icons and simple graphics, where 256 colours are plenty and the file shrinks a lot. For a normal photo, leave PNG-8 unticked, because a photo needs far more than 256 colours to look smooth. If the PNG is bigger than the WebP you started from, that is normal: PNG does not throw away detail the way WebP does.
content.limit: Only WebP images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. A PNG file is usually bigger than the WebP it came from, because PNG keeps every pixel. PNG-8 keeps only 256 colours, so smooth photos may show banding. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 WebP photo gives a 1200 by 800 PNG file with the same picture, ready to edit or print.
faq: Why is the PNG bigger than my WebP?

PNG keeps every pixel exactly, while WebP throws away detail to save space. A photo converted to PNG is usually bigger than the WebP it came from. Tick PNG-8 if you want a smaller file and 256 colours are enough.
Does PNG keep the transparency from WebP?
Yes. WebP can hold transparency, and PNG keeps it. The see-through parts stay see-through in the PNG. Convert to JPG instead only if you want a solid background.
When is PNG-8 the right choice?
PNG-8 suits logos, icons and simple graphics, where 256 colours are plenty and the file shrinks a lot. For a normal photo, leave PNG-8 unticked, because a photo needs far more colours to look smooth.
Does the PNG match the WebP size?
Yes. The width and height stay exactly the same as the WebP. Only the file format changes. Use Image Resizer if you also need a different size.

short.en: Turn JPG images into WebP.

tools.meta_description: Turn JPG images into WebP in your browser, free and private. Smaller files for the web.
steps: Choose a JPG image with the file button.
Set the quality with the slider, or tick Best quality for the sharpest result.
Type a target size in KB if the file must fit under a limit.
Press Convert JPG to WebP.
Save the downloaded WebP, which has the same width and height as the JPG.

content.use: JPG to WebP turns a JPG picture into a WebP file, keeping the same width and height. A shop owner turns JPG product photos into WebP so the online shop loads faster, because WebP is smaller than JPG at the same quality. WebP opens in all modern browsers and most phones, so it is the right choice for the web. The quality slider trades a little sharpness for a smaller file, and the target size mode lowers the quality step by step until the file fits. Photos are turned the right way up from their photo data. The picture is converted in your browser, so your image is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Use a quality of 80 to 90 for photos on a website: the file shrinks a lot and the picture still looks sharp. If a portal asks for a file under a certain size, type that size in the target size box and let the tool lower the quality until it fits. Best quality is for pictures you want to keep, not for pictures you will upload.
content.limit: Only JPG images are accepted, and each file must be under 50 MB. Browsers cannot save true lossless WebP, so Best quality saves at the highest lossy quality instead. Very old programs may not open WebP; use JPG instead if the other side is old. The picture keeps its original width and height; this tool does not resize it.
content.example: Converting a 1200 by 800 JPG photo at quality 85 gives a 1200 by 800 WebP file that is roughly a third smaller and looks the same.
faq: How much smaller is WebP than JPG?
At the same quality, WebP is usually 25 to 35 percent smaller than JPG. The exact saving depends on the picture: a photo with lots of detail saves less than a plain one.
What does Best quality actually do?
It saves at quality 100, the highest setting a browser canvas offers. Browsers cannot save true lossless WebP, so Best quality is the sharpest lossy result, not a perfect copy of the JPG.
What if the file still does not fit my target size?
The tool lowers the quality step by step down to 10 percent. If the file still does not fit, make the picture smaller with Image Resizer first, then convert it again with the same target size.
Does WebP open everywhere JPG does?
No. WebP opens in all modern browsers and most phones, but very old programs may not know it. If the other side is old or you are not sure, send a JPG instead.

short.en: Turn SVG files into PNG images.

tools.meta_description: Turn SVG files into PNG images in your browser, free and private. Choose the output width.
steps: Choose an SVG file with the file button.
Pick 1x, 2x or 3x scale, or type an exact width and height in pixels. An icon size like 512 gives you a square image.
Choose the background: transparent, white, or a colour you pick. JPG always uses a solid background.
Choose PNG, JPG, WebP or AVIF as the output format.
Press Convert SVG to PNG and save the downloaded image, which has the size you chose and the same shape as the SVG.

content.use: SVG to PNG turns a vector drawing into a normal picture file you can use anywhere. You can scale it to 1x, 2x or 3x its own size, type an exact width and height, or pick a ready icon size from 16 up to 512 pixels, which is handy for app icons and favicons. The background can stay transparent for logos, or you can fill it white or with a colour you choose, and the result can be saved as PNG, JPG, WebP or AVIF. The SVG is read from its own width, height and viewBox, so the shape never stretches. Everything runs in your browser and the file is never uploaded.
content.tip: For a crisp icon, pick 2x or 3x scale instead of a small exact size. For a logo on a coloured page, keep the background transparent and use PNG.
content.limit: An SVG that loads pictures or fonts from the internet cannot be converted here, because the browser blocks those outside files. Very detailed SVGs can be slow to draw at large sizes.
content.example: A 200 pixel wide logo scaled to 3x becomes a sharp 600 pixel PNG, ready to paste into a presentation or a document.
faq: What size should I pick
Use 1x for the size the SVG was drawn at, 2x or 3x when you need it sharper on high resolution screens, and an exact width when another app asks for a set number of pixels.
Can I keep the background clear
Yes. Choose transparent as the background and PNG or WebP as the format, and the empty parts of the image stay see through. JPG cannot be transparent, so it always fills the background with white.
Why did my SVG fail

The most common cause is an SVG that loads a picture or a font from a web address, which the browser blocks for safety. Save those pictures inside the SVG file itself, or remove the outside links, and try again.
What are icon sizes for
Icon sizes give you square pictures at the standard sizes apps and websites expect, from 16 pixels for a tiny favicon up to 512 pixels for a large app icon. Pick the size the app or site asks for.

short.en: Crop an image to the part you need.

tools.meta_description: Crop an image in your browser, free and private. Drag to choose the area, then download a PNG.
steps: Choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image with the file button.
Drag the corners of the box on the preview to choose the part you want to keep, or type the exact numbers in the X, Y, Width and Height boxes.
Pick an aspect ratio like 1 to 1 or 16 to 9, or tick Lock ratio to keep the box shape while you drag it.
Use Straighten to fix a tilted photo, Rotate to turn it, and Flip to mirror it. Then choose the output format and quality.
Press Crop Image and save the downloaded picture, which holds only the part you chose.

content.use: Image Cropper cuts a picture down to just the part you need, right in your browser. You drag a box over the photo to choose what stays, and you can lock the box to a shape like square, 16 to 9 or 3 to 2, which is handy for profile pictures and social media posts. If the photo is tilted, the straighten slider levels it, and the rotate and flip buttons turn or mirror it without leaving the page. You can type exact pixel numbers when you need a precise cut, and you choose PNG, JPG or WebP for the result. Nothing is uploaded, so your photo stays on your device.
content.tip: Pick the aspect ratio before you drag, so the box keeps the right shape. For a profile picture, use 1 to 1 and keep the face in the middle of the box.
content.limit: The cropper needs the Cropper.js library from the internet, so it will not start when you are offline. Very large images are slowed down by the browser, so keep the file under 50 MB.
content.example: A wide holiday photo cropped to 1 to 1 keeps just the people in the middle, ready to use as a profile picture on any site.
faq: How do I crop to a square
Choose 1 to 1 from the aspect ratio list, then drag the box over the part you want. The box stays square while you move it, and the result is a square picture.
What does lock ratio do
Lock ratio keeps the box in its current shape while you drag a corner, so the width and height change together. Unticking it lets you drag the box freely to any shape you like.
Can I straighten a tilted photo
Yes. Move the straighten slider left or right until the horizon or the lines in the photo look level, then press Crop Image. The photo is turned by that many degrees before it is cut.
Which format keeps the best quality
PNG keeps every pixel exactly and is best for screenshots and graphics. JPG is smaller for photos, and 92 percent quality looks the same as the original on screen. WebP sits between the two.

short.en: Rotate or flip an image in your browser.

tools.meta_description: Rotate or flip an image in your browser, free and private. Turn it left or right, or mirror it.
steps: Choose one or more JPG, PNG or WebP images with the file button. Phone photos are turned the right way up from their EXIF details.
Press Rotate Left or Rotate Right to turn the picture in 90 degree steps, or Flip Horizontal or Flip Vertical to mirror it.
Move the Straighten slider to fix a tilted photo by a few degrees, up to 45 each way.
Pick the output format, PNG, JPG or WebP, in the Output format box.
Press Download Image. One picture downloads at once, and several pictures download together as a ZIP.

content.use: Rotate and Flip Image turns, mirrors and straightens your pictures without uploading them. You can rotate in 90 degree steps, flip a photo left to right or top to bottom, and use the straighten slider to fix a horizon that is a few degrees off, which is handy for photos taken at a slight tilt. Phone photos are read the right way up automatically from their EXIF details, so a sideways picture is fixed before you start. You can work on several images at once and download them together as a ZIP, and you choose PNG, JPG or WebP for the result. Everything happens in your browser, so your photos stay private.
content.tip: Straighten works best on small tilts. Turn the photo with Rotate first to get it close, then use the slider for the last few degrees.
content.limit: Rotation is exact for 90 degree steps. Straightening turns the picture by a few degrees and fills the corners with the image edge, so a small part of the corners is lost. TIFF files are not accepted here.
content.example: A photo saved sideways by a phone is fixed by the EXIF check, then flipped horizontally so the text in it reads the right way.
faq: Why is my photo sideways

Phones save the photo as it was taken and note the right way up in the EXIF details. This tool reads those details and turns the photo the right way up when it loads, so you rarely need to rotate it yourself.
Can I rotate by any angle
Yes. Rotate Left and Rotate Right turn the picture in 90 degree steps, and the straighten slider adds up to 45 degrees each way. Together they cover any angle you need.
Does flipping lose quality
No. Flipping and 90 degree rotation only move the pixels around, so nothing is lost. Saving as JPG compresses the picture again, so use PNG when you want the pixels kept exactly as they are.
Can I rotate many photos together
Yes. Choose several images at once, set the rotation and flip once, then press Download Image. Every photo gets the same change, and the results download together as one ZIP file.

short.en: Make a passport photo at the right size.

tools.meta_description: Make a passport photo at the right size for Pakistan, India, USA, UK, EU, UAE or Canada, in your browser.
steps: Choose a clear photo of your face with the file button.
Pick your country, or NADRA CNIC / NICOP, or the Punjab driving licence.
Line your head up inside the guide oval on the preview.
Press Make Passport Photo and save the downloaded photo.
Press Download Print Sheet if you want several copies on one sheet to print.

content.use: Passport Photo Maker cuts your photo to the exact size a passport, ID card or driving licence asks for. It makes 35 by 45 mm photos for a Pakistan passport, a NADRA CNIC or a Punjab driving licence. The preview shows a guide oval for your head and a line for your shoulders, so you can see the framing before you save. NADRA photos are saved small enough for Pak-ID online, and a print sheet puts 4 or 6 photos on a 4 by 6 inch sheet, or 8 on a 6 by 8 inch sheet. The photo is cut in your browser, so your picture is never uploaded anywhere and you do not need an account.
content.tip: Take the photo against a plain white wall in daylight, with your face straight at the camera and no glasses on. Keep your head inside the guide oval and your shoulders on the shoulder line. For NADRA, the photo must be taken within the last 6 months, and the file must be 60 KB or smaller, which the tool handles for you.
content.limit: Photos up to 50 MB are accepted. The tool cuts the middle of your photo to the chosen size, so a photo taken too close or too far may cut off part of your head. It cannot fix a blurry or dark photo, and it cannot remove glasses or a background that is not white. A print sheet is only offered for 35 by 45 mm photos, because a bigger photo does not fit a 4 by 6 or 6 by 8 sheet at exact size.
content.example: A 2000 by 1500 photo of your face becomes a 413 by 531 px passport photo, 35 by 45 mm at 300 DPI, ready to print or upload.
faq: What size is a NADRA CNIC photo?
35 by 45 mm, which is 413 by 531 pixels at 300 DPI. The head must be 31.5 to 36 mm high, the background must be plain white, and the photo must be taken within the last 6 months.
Why is my NADRA file saved at lower quality?

Pak-ID online takes a file of 60 KB or less. The tool lowers the quality step by step until the file fits, and tells you the final size. If it still does not fit at the lowest quality, take a plainer photo with less detail.
Does the guide oval appear in the saved photo?
No. The guide oval and shoulder line are only on the preview, to help you frame your head. The downloaded photo is clean, with no lines or marks on it.
How many photos fit on one print sheet?
4 or 6 photos fit on a 4 by 6 inch sheet, and 8 fit on a 6 by 8 inch sheet. 8 photos do not fit on a 4 by 6 sheet at exact size, so the tool uses the bigger sheet for 8.

short.en: Convert length, weight, temperature, pressure and more.

tools.meta_description: Convert length, weight, temperature, area, volume, speed, data, time, energy, pressure, power, fuel economy and cooking units in your browser.
steps: Choose the kind of unit in the 'Unit type' list, such as Length, Pressure, Energy, Power, Fuel or Cooking.
Type the number in the 'Value' box. The result updates as you type, and shows every unit of that kind at once.
Choose the unit you have in the 'From' list and the unit you want in the 'To' list, or press Swap to reverse them.
In Cooking mode, pick an ingredient to change grams into cups, or cups into grams.
Your recent conversions are kept under the result, so you can tap one to run it again.

content.use: Unit Converter changes a measurement from one unit to another in your browser. A student changes 5 kilometres into metres for homework. A driver checks fuel use in miles per gallon against litres per 100 km. A cook changes 250 grams of flour into cups. Typing a value shows every unit of that kind at once, so 5 km shows metres, miles and feet together. Common pairs are one tap away, and recent conversions are remembered in this browser.
content.tip: In Cooking mode, pick the ingredient first: one cup of flour weighs about 120 grams but one cup of sugar weighs about 200 grams, so the answer changes. For fuel, remember that a smaller litres-per-100-km number means better economy, while a bigger miles-per-gallon number does. Press Swap to reverse a conversion instead of retyping it.
content.limit: Cooking cup weights are estimates from common density tables, not exact measurements, and are labelled as estimates. Recent conversions are stored only in this browser, at most 8 of them, and are lost if you clear site data. Data units use 1024 per step, not 1000, and volume uses US measures.
content.example: Choosing Pressure and typing 1 bar shows 100 kPa, 14.5 psi and 0.987 atm at once. Choosing Energy, 1 kWh shows 3.6 MJ. Choosing Power, 1 hp shows about 745.7 W. In Cooking mode, 120 grams of flour shows about 1 cup.
faq: How do I convert bar to kilopascals?
Choose Pressure, type the number, pick bar in the From list and kilopascal in the To list. 1 bar equals 100 kPa, and the all-units view shows psi and atm at the same time.
What does the cooking mode do?

Cooking mode changes grams into cups, or cups into grams, using a density table for each ingredient, because one cup of flour does not weigh the same as one cup of sugar. The weights are estimates and are labelled as such.
Can I see all units at once?
Yes. As soon as you type a value, the result lists every unit of the chosen kind together, so 5 kilometres shows metres, miles, feet and yards in one view.
Does the converter remember my recent conversions?
Yes. Your last 8 conversions are kept in this browser under the result, and tapping one runs it again. They are stored only on your device and disappear if you clear site data.

short.en: Work out sale prices and savings.

tools.meta_description: Work out the discount amount and the final sale price from any price and percent.
steps: Type the original price in the 'Original price' box.
Type the discount percent in the 'Discount (%)' box.
Press Calculate Discount, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the discount amount and the final price under the button.

content.use: Discount Calculator works out how much you save in a sale and what you actually pay. A shopper sees a shirt marked 20 percent off and wants the real price before buying. A shop owner sets a sale price that still leaves a profit. A student checks whether a 50 percent off deal is really half price. You type the original price and the discount percent, and the tool shows the discount amount and the price you pay. It works for any currency, because it only uses the numbers you type.
content.tip: A 20 percent discount means you pay 80 percent of the price, so you can check the answer by working out 80 percent of the price. For two discounts in a row, apply the first discount, then apply the second discount to the new price, not to the original price. Round the final price to your local currency before you pay.
content.limit: The discount percent must be between 0 and 100. The tool does not add tax or delivery charges, so the price it shows is before tax. It only uses the numbers you type, so check that the original price is right.
content.example: A price of 1000 with a 20 percent discount gives a discount of 200 and a final price of 800.
faq: How do I find the price after discount?
Type the original price and the discount percent, then press Calculate Discount. The final price is shown next to the discount amount.
What is 25 percent off 400?
The discount is 100 and the final price is 300. Type 400 as the price and 25 as the discount percent to see it.
Can the discount be more than 100 percent?
No. A discount above 100 percent would make the price negative, so the tool only accepts 0 to 100 percent.
Does it add tax to the price?
No. The tool shows the price before tax. Add your local tax to the final price yourself if you need the total you will pay.

short.en: See how savings grow over time.

tools.meta_description: See how savings grow with compound interest over years, with any compounding frequency.
steps: Type the starting amount in the 'Principal amount' box.
Type the yearly interest rate in the 'Annual interest rate (%)' box.
Type the number of years and choose how often interest is added in the 'Compounding' list.
Press Calculate Compound Interest, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the maturity amount and the interest earned under the button.

content.use: Compound Interest Calculator shows how savings grow when the interest itself earns interest. A saver puts money in a bank account and wants to know what it becomes in 5 years. A parent plans a fund for a child and compares yearly and monthly compounding. A student learns why starting early matters more than saving more later. You type the starting amount, the yearly rate, the years, and how often interest is added, and the tool shows the final amount and the interest earned.
content.tip: Monthly compounding grows slightly faster than yearly compounding at the same rate, because interest starts earning interest sooner. The rate you type should be the yearly rate the bank quotes. This tool assumes you add no more money and take nothing out during the years.
content.limit: The tool assumes a fixed rate and no deposits or withdrawals after the start. Real bank rates change, and tax or fees are not included, so the result is an estimate. The rate must be 0 or more and the years must be more than 0.
content.example: 100,000 at 10 percent a year for 5 years, compounded yearly, grows to 161,051, with 61,051 interest earned.
faq: What is compound interest?
It is interest earned on both the starting amount and the interest already added. Each time interest is added, the next interest is worked out on the bigger amount.
Is monthly compounding better than yearly?
Yes, slightly. With monthly compounding the interest starts earning interest sooner, so the same rate gives a slightly bigger final amount.
Does it include tax on the interest?
No. The tool shows the amount before tax. Your bank or tax office may take tax from the interest, so the money you keep can be less.
Can I add monthly deposits with this tool?
No. This tool works out growth on one starting amount only. It does not add regular deposits or withdrawals, so use a savings plan calculator if you add money every month.

short.en: Monthly home loan payment, with tax, insurance and HOA.

tools.meta_description: Work out your monthly home loan payment, free in your browser. Principal and interest plus property tax, insurance and HOA, with a full schedule and a 20-year vs 30-year comparison.
steps: Type the loan amount in the 'Loan amount' box.
Type the yearly interest rate in the 'Annual interest rate (%)' box.
Type the loan length in years in the 'Loan term (years)' box.
Type your monthly property tax, insurance and HOA, if any — these are added to the monthly payment.

Add an extra monthly payment or a lump sum if you plan to pay more, and tick Compare 20-year vs 30-year to see both terms side by side. Press Calculate Monthly Payment, or just wait, because the result updates as you type. The full month-by-month schedule appears below, and Download Schedule (CSV) saves it.

content.use: Mortgage Calculator works out the monthly payment on a home loan. A buyer checks whether the monthly payment fits the family budget before choosing a house. A family compares a 20 year loan with a 30 year loan to see the difference in payment and total interest. An owner checks how much of each payment goes to interest in the early years. You type the loan amount, the yearly interest rate and the years, and the tool shows the monthly payment, the total paid and the total interest. Property tax, insurance and HOA are typed in as monthly amounts and added to the payment, so you see the full monthly cost. The schedule shows how much of each payment is interest in the early years, and the 20-year vs 30-year comparison shows the trade-off between a lower payment and more total interest.
content.tip: A longer loan means a smaller monthly payment but much more total interest, so compare both numbers before you choose. A small rise in the rate can add a lot to the monthly payment on a big loan. Type your real monthly property tax, insurance and HOA so the total monthly payment is the full cost, not just principal and interest.
content.limit: The payment shown is principal and interest, plus the monthly property tax, insurance and HOA amounts you type in. It does not include other charges your lender may add, such as mortgage insurance or a variable rate. The rate is assumed fixed for the whole loan, so a variable rate loan will differ. Property tax, insurance and HOA are your own figures — the tool does not look them up.
content.example: A loan of 5,000,000 at 12 percent a year for 20 years gives a monthly payment of 55,054.31. With property tax 10,000, insurance 3,000 and HOA 2,000 a month, the total monthly payment is 70,054.31.
faq: How is the monthly payment worked out?
It uses the standard loan formula with the yearly rate divided by 12 and the number of monthly payments. The payment stays the same every month for a fixed rate loan.
Why is the total interest so high?
Interest is charged on the amount you still owe, which is large in the early years. Over 20 years the interest adds up to a large share of the total paid.
Does it include property tax?

Yes, if you type it in. Property tax, insurance and HOA are separate boxes, and the amounts you enter are added to the monthly payment. The tool does not look up your local tax or insurance rates — use the figures from your own bills or lender.
What happens if the rate changes?
This tool assumes a fixed rate. If your loan has a variable rate, the monthly payment will change when the rate changes, so work it out again with the new rate.

short.en: Split the bill and work out the tip.

tools.meta_description: Work out the tip, the total bill and the amount each person pays when you split it.
steps: Type the bill amount in the 'Bill amount' box.
Type the tip percent in the 'Tip (%)' box.
Type the number of people in the 'Split between (people)' box.
Press Calculate Tip, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the tip, the total and the amount per person under the button.

content.use: Tip Calculator works out the tip on a restaurant bill and splits the total fairly. Friends share a dinner bill and want to know what each person pays with the tip included. A traveller in another country wants to leave the right tip without doing the maths by hand. A family checks the total before paying by card. You type the bill, the tip percent and the number of people, and the tool shows the tip, the total and the amount per person.
content.tip: A 10 percent tip is easy to check: move the decimal point one place left on the bill. If the service was poor, you can set the tip to 0 and just split the bill. In some countries a service charge is already added to the bill, so check before you tip on top of it.
content.limit: The tip percent must be 0 or more and the number of people must be at least 1. The tool does not add tax, so use the bill amount before or after tax as you prefer. Amounts are rounded to 2 decimal places, so a few cents may differ when you split.
content.example: A bill of 2000 with a 15 percent tip and 4 people gives a tip of 300, a total of 2300, and 575 per person.
faq: How much should I tip at a restaurant?
It depends on the country. In many places 10 to 15 percent is common, and 15 to 20 percent is common in the United States. Check local custom before you tip.
How do I split a bill between friends?
Type the bill, the tip percent and the number of people. The tool shows the amount each person pays, including the tip.
Does the tip include tax?
No. The tool works out the tip on the bill amount you type. If you want the tip on the amount before tax, type the bill before tax.
Can I tip 0 percent?
Yes. Set the tip to 0 and the tool splits just the bill. The tip amount shows as 0 and the total is the same as the bill.

short.en: Convert times between world time zones.

tools.meta_description: Convert a date and time between world time zones, with daylight saving handled.
steps: Pick the date in the 'Date' box and the time in the 'Time' box.
Choose the zone the time is in, in the 'From time zone' list.
Choose the zone you want in the 'To time zone' list.
Press Convert Time Zone, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the converted date and time under the button.

content.use: Time Zone Converter changes a time from one part of the world to another. A worker in Lahore joins a call with a team in London and needs the right time. A student applies to a university abroad and must not miss a deadline in another time zone. A family calls relatives overseas and wants to avoid waking them up. You pick the date and time, choose the zone you have and the zone you want, and the tool shows the converted time, with daylight saving handled for you.
content.tip: Daylight saving changes the gap between zones in summer and winter, so always include the date, not just the time. London is 5 hours behind Lahore in winter but 4 hours behind in summer. If the converted time falls on another day, the tool shows the new date too.
content.limit: The tool uses the time zone rules built into your browser, which are kept up to date by your system. Very old or future dates may use rules that have changed. It converts clock times only; it does not book meetings or send invites.
content.example: 12:00 on 15 January 2026 in Lahore is 07:00 on 15 January 2026 in London.
faq: What is the time difference between Lahore and London?
It is 5 hours in winter and 4 hours in summer, because London uses daylight saving and Lahore does not. Pick a date to get the right gap.
Does it handle daylight saving time?
Yes. The tool uses your browser's time zone rules, so daylight saving is applied for the date you pick, and the gap between two zones can change with the season.
Can I convert to New York time?
Yes. Choose America/New_York in the To list. New York is 10 hours behind Lahore in winter and 9 hours behind in summer.
Why does the date change sometimes?
When the converted time crosses midnight, the date moves to the next day or the day before. The tool always shows the full date with the time.

short.en: Count days, weeks and months between dates.

tools.meta_description: Count the days, weeks and months between any two dates in your browser.
steps: Pick the first date in the 'From date' box.
Pick the second date in the 'To date' box.
Press Calculate Difference, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read the days, weeks and months under the button.

content.use: Date Difference Calculator counts the time between two dates. A worker counts the days left before a project deadline. A parent counts the days until a child's birthday. A student counts the weeks between the start and the end of a term. A traveller counts the days of a trip. You pick the two dates and the tool shows the days between them, the weeks and days, and the full months, so you can plan without counting on a calendar.
content.tip: The count is the number of days from the first date to the second date, not including the first date. If you need to include both end days, add 1 to the day count. The order of the two dates does not matter; the tool always counts the gap between them.
content.limit: The tool counts whole days between the dates you pick. It does not count working days or skip weekends and holidays. Very old dates may use calendar rules that differ from today's calendar.
content.example: From 1 January 2025 to 1 January 2026 is 365 days, which is 52 weeks and 1 day.
faq: How many days are between two dates?
Pick the two dates and press Calculate Difference. The tool shows the exact number of days, plus the weeks and days and the full months.
Does it count the first date?
No. The count is the days from the first date to the second date. If you want to include both end days, add 1 to the day count.
Can I count weeks instead of days?
Yes. The result shows the weeks and the extra days as well, so 365 days shows as 52 weeks and 1 day.
Does the order of the dates matter?
No. The tool always counts the gap between the two dates, whichever one you pick first, so you can enter them in any order you like.

short.en: Work out your daily calorie needs.

tools.meta_description: Estimate your BMR and daily calorie needs (TDEE) from age, height, weight and activity.
steps: Type your age in the 'Age (years)' box.
Choose your sex in the 'Sex' list and type your height and weight.
Choose your activity level in the 'Activity level' list.
Press Calculate Calories, or just wait, because the result updates as you type.
Read your BMR and TDEE in calories a day under the button.

content.use: Calorie and TDEE Calculator estimates how many calories your body uses in a day. A person starting a diet wants a daily target that fits their body and activity. A gym member checks whether they eat enough to build muscle. A student learns the difference between BMR, the calories the body uses at rest, and TDEE, the total with daily activity. You type your age, sex, height and weight, choose your activity level, and the tool shows your BMR and TDEE.
content.tip: TDEE is the number to use for a daily calorie target, not BMR, because BMR leaves out all movement. Choose the activity level that matches a normal week, not your busiest day. A small change in weight or activity changes the result, so update the numbers as they change.
content.limit: These numbers are estimates from the Mifflin-St Jeor formula, not medical advice. They do not fit everyone, including children, pregnant people, and people with some health conditions. For a personal diet or health plan, talk to a doctor or a qualified dietitian.
content.example: A 30-year-old man, 180 cm tall and 80 kg, moderately active, has a BMR of 1780 calories a day and a TDEE of 2759 calories a day.
faq: What is the difference between BMR and TDEE?
BMR is the calories your body uses at rest to stay alive. TDEE adds your daily activity and movement, so it is the total calories you use in a day.
How many calories do I need to lose weight?
Most people aim for a TDEE minus about 300 to 500 calories a day. This tool only gives the estimate; a doctor or dietitian can set a safe target for you.
Which activity level should I choose?
Pick the level that matches a normal week. Desk work with little exercise is sedentary, while a physical job or daily training is very active.
Is this medical advice?
No. The numbers are estimates from a standard formula. They are not a diagnosis or a diet plan, so talk to a doctor for personal advice.

short.en: Sin, cos, log, powers and more.

tools.meta_description: A free scientific calculator with sin, cos, tan, log, square root and powers.
steps: Tap the number and operator keys to build your sum in the display.
Tap a function key such as sin, cos, log or sqrt to add it to the sum.
Tap the pi or e key when you need those numbers.
Press = to work out the answer, or C to clear the display.
Read the result under the display.

content.use: Scientific Calculator does the maths a basic calculator cannot. A student works out sin of 30 degrees for a trigonometry problem.
